यवीयसी तयोर्या तु यमी कन्या यशस्विनी ॥
5.35.m: The lord performs terrible austerity on the ridge of Mount Meru even today. / The younger of the two, the renowned daughter Yamī,

5.35.s:
abhavatsā saricchreṣṭhā yamunā lokapā vanī |
manurityucyate loke sāvarṇiriti cocyate ||
5.35.d:
अभवत्सा सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा यमुना लोकपा वनी ।
मनुरित्युच्यते लोके सावर्णिरिति चोच्यते ॥
5.35.m: became the Yamunā, the best of rivers, the purifier of the world. / He is called Manu in the world, and he is called Sāvarṇi.

5.35.s:
ya idaṃ janma devānāṃ śṛṇuyāddhārayettu vā |
āpadaṃ prāpya mucyeta prāpnuyātsumahadyaśaḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.35.d:
य इदं जन्म देवानां शृणुयाद्धारयेत्तु वा ।
आपदं प्राप्य मुच्येत प्राप्नुयात्सुमहद्यशः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.35.m:
Whoever hears or retains this birth of the gods / is freed when encountering distress and attains exceedingly great renown.

Homage to the glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.36.s:
sūta uvāca |
manorvaivasvatasyāsanputrā vai nava tatsamāḥ |
paścānmahonnatā dhīrāḥ kṣatradharmaparāyaṇāḥ ||
5.36.d:
सूत उवाच ।
मनोर्वैवस्वतस्यासन्पुत्रा वै नव तत्समाः ।
पश्चान्महोन्नता धीराः क्षत्रधर्मपरायणाः ॥
5.36.m: Sūta said: / Manu Vaivasvata had nine sons equal to him, / later exceedingly exalted, steadfast, devoted to the duty of the kṣatriyas:

5.36.s:
ikṣvākuḥ śibinābhāgau dhṛṣṭaḥ śaryātireva ca |
nariṣyanto'tha nābhāgaḥ karūṣaśca priyavrataḥ ||
5.36.d:
इक्ष्वाकुः शिबिनाभागौ धृष्टः शर्यातिरेव च ।
नरिष्यन्तोऽथ नाभागः करूषश्च प्रियव्रतः ॥
5.36.m: Ikṣvāku, Śibi, Nābhāga, Dhṛṣṭa, and Śaryāti, / Nariṣyanta, then Nābhāga, Karūṣa, and Priyavrata.

5.36.s:
akarotputrakāmastu manuriṣṭiṃ prajāpatiḥ |
anutpanneṣu putreṣu tatreṣṭyāṃ munipuṅgavaḥ ||
5.36.d:
अकरोत्पुत्रकामस्तु मनुरिष्टिं प्रजापतिः ।
अनुत्पन्नेषु पुत्रेषु तत्रेष्ट्यां मुनिपुङ्गवः ॥
5.36.m: Desiring a son, the Prajāpati Manu performed a sacrifice / when no sons had yet been born, at which sacrifice, O best of sages,

5.36.s:
sā hi divyāmbaradharā divyābharaṇabhūṣitā |
divyasaṃhananā caivamilā jajñe hi viśrutā ||
5.36.d:
सा हि दिव्याम्बरधरा दिव्याभरणभूषिता ।
दिव्यसंहनना चैवमिला जज्ञे हि विश्रुता ॥
5.36.m: wearing celestial garments, adorned with celestial ornaments, / and of celestial physique, the renowned Ilā was born.

5.36.s:
tāmiḍetyeva hovāca manurdaṇḍadharastathā |
anugacchasva māmeti tamiḍā pratyuvāca ha ||
5.36.d:
तामिडेत्येव होवाच मनुर्दण्डधरस्तथा ।
अनुगच्छस्व मामेति तमिडा प्रत्युवाच ह ॥
5.36.m: Manu, the rod-bearer, said to her: "O Iḍā, / follow me!" Then Iḍā replied to him,

5.36.s:
dharmayuktamidaṃ vākyaṃ putrakāmaṃ prajāpatim |
iḍovāca |
mitrāvaruṇayoraṃśairjātāsmi vadatāṃ vara ||
5.36.d:
धर्मयुक्तमिदं वाक्यं पुत्रकामं प्रजापतिम् ।
इडोवाच ।
मित्रावरुणयोरंशैर्जातास्मि वदतां वर ॥
5.36.m: this righteous statement to the Prajāpati who desired a son. / Iḍā said: / "I was born from the portions of Mitra and Varuṇa, O best of speakers.

5.36.s:
tayoḥ sakāśaṃ yāsyāmi na me'dharme rucirbhavet |
evamuktvā satī sā tu mitrāvaruṇayostataḥ ||
5.36.d:
तयोः सकाशं यास्यामि न मेऽधर्मे रुचिर्भवेत् ।
एवमुक्त्वा सती सा तु मित्रावरुणयोस्ततः ॥
5.36.m: I shall go to their presence; may I have no inclination toward unrighteousness." / Having spoken thus, the virtuous woman of shapely hips then,

5.36.s:
gatvāntikaṃ varārohā prāñjalirvākyamabravīt |
aṃśaistu yuvayorjātā manuyajñe mahāmunī ||
5.36.d:
गत्वान्तिकं वरारोहा प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ।
अंशैस्तु युवयोर्जाता मनुयज्ञे महामुनी ॥
5.36.m: having approached Mitra and Varuṇa, said with folded palms: / "I was born from portions of you two in Manu's sacrifice, O great sages.

5.36.s:
āgatā bhavatoranti brūtaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi vām |
anyān putrān sṛja vibho tairvaṃśaste bhaviṣyati ||
5.36.d:
आगता भवतोरन्ति ब्रूतं किं करवाणि वाम् ।
अन्यान् पुत्रान् सृज विभो तैर्वंशस्ते भविष्यति ॥
5.36.m: I have come before you two; tell me what I should do for you both. / Create other sons, O lord; through them your lineage will be established."

5.36.s:
sūta uvāca |
tāṃ tathāvādinīṃ sādhvīmiḍāṃ manvadhvarodbhavām |
mitrāvaruṇanāmānau munī ūcaturādarāt ||
5.36.d:
सूत उवाच ।
तां तथावादिनीं साध्वीमिडां मन्वध्वरोद्भवाम् ।
मित्रावरुणनामानौ मुनी ऊचतुरादरात् ॥
5.36.m: Sūta said: / To that virtuous Iḍā, who spoke thus and was born of Manu's sacrifice, / the two sages named Mitra and Varuṇa said with respect:

5.36.s:
mitrāvaruṇāvūcatuḥ |
anena tava dharmajñe praśrayeṇa damena ca |
satyena caiva suśroṇi prītau dvau varavarṇini ||
5.36.d:
मित्रावरुणावूचतुः ।
अनेन तव धर्मज्ञे प्रश्रयेण दमेन च ।
सत्येन चैव सुश्रोणि प्रीतौ द्वौ वरवर्णिनि ॥
5.36.m: Mitra and Varuṇa said: / "By this modesty, self-control, / and truthfulness of yours, O knower of righteousness, O fair-hipped, beautiful woman, we two are pleased.

5.36.s:
āvayostvaṃ mahābhāge khyātiṃ caiva gamiṣyasi |
manorvaṃśakaraḥ putrastvameva ca bhaviṣyasi ||
5.36.d:
आवयोस्त्वं महाभागे ख्यातिं चैव गमिष्यसि ।
मनोर्वंशकरः पुत्रस्त्वमेव च भविष्यसि ॥
5.36.m: You will attain renown through the two of us, O highly fortunate one, / and you yourself will become the son who continues Manu's lineage,

5.36.s:
sudyumna iti vikhyātastriṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ |
jagatpriyo dharmaśīlau manuvaṃśavivardhanaḥ ||
5.36.d:
सुद्युम्न इति विख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः ।
जगत्प्रियो धर्मशीलौ मनुवंशविवर्धनः ॥
5.36.m: renowned as Sudyumna, famed throughout the three worlds, / dear to the world, righteous in nature, the expander of Manu's lineage."

5.36.s:
sūta uvāca |
nivṛttā sā tu tacchrutvā gacchantī piturantike |
budhenāntaramāsādya maithunāyopamantritā ||
5.36.d:
सूत उवाच ।
निवृत्ता सा तु तच्छ्रुत्वा गच्छन्ती पितुरन्तिके ।
बुधेनान्तरमासाद्य मैथुनायोपमन्त्रिता ॥
5.36.m: Sūta said: / Having heard that, she turned back, and while going to her father's presence, / finding an opportunity, she was invited by Budha for intercourse.

5.36.s:
somaputrāttato jajñe tasyāṃ rājā purūravāḥ |
putro'tisundaraḥ prājña urvaśīpatirunnataḥ ||
5.36.d:
सोमपुत्रात्ततो जज्ञे तस्यां राजा पुरूरवाः ।
पुत्रोऽतिसुन्दरः प्राज्ञ उर्वशीपतिरुन्नतः ॥
5.36.m: Then from the son of Soma was born in her King Purūravas, / a most handsome, wise, exalted son, the husband of Urvaśī.

5.36.s:
janayitvā ca sā tatra purūravasamādarāt |
putraṃ śivaprasādāttu punaḥ sudyumnatāṃ gataḥ ||
5.36.d:
जनयित्वा च सा तत्र पुरूरवसमादरात् ।
पुत्रं शिवप्रसादात्तु पुनः सुद्युम्नतां गतः ॥
5.36.m: And after giving birth to Purūravas there with respect, / she became the son Sudyumna once again by the grace of Śiva.

5.36.s:
sudyumnasya tu dāyādāstrayaḥ paramadhārmikāḥ |
utkalaśca gayaścāpi vinatāśvaśca vīryavān ||
5.36.d:
सुद्युम्नस्य तु दायादास्त्रयः परमधार्मिकाः ।
उत्कलश्च गयश्चापि विनताश्वश्च वीर्यवान् ॥
5.36.m: Sudyumna had three heirs who were supremely righteous: / Utkala, Gaya, and the mighty Vinatāśva.

5.36.s:
utkalasyotkalā viprā vinatāśvasya paścimā |
dikpūrvā muniśārdūla gayasya tu gayā smṛtā ||
5.36.d:
उत्कलस्योत्कला विप्रा विनताश्वस्य पश्चिमा ।
दिक्पूर्वा मुनिशार्दूल गयस्य तु गया स्मृता ॥
5.36.m: Utkalā belongs to Utkala, O brahmins; the western quarter to Vinatāśva; / the eastern quarter, O tiger among sages, and Gayā are remembered as Gaya's.

5.36.s:
praviṣṭe tu manau tāta divākaratanuṃ tadā |
daśadhā tatra tatkṣetramakarotpṛthivīmimām ||
5.36.d:
प्रविष्टे तु मनौ तात दिवाकरतनुं तदा ।
दशधा तत्र तत्क्षेत्रमकरोत्पृथिवीमिमाम् ॥
5.36.m: When Manu entered the body of the Sun at that time, O dear one, / he divided this earth, that domain, into ten parts.

5.36.s:
ikṣvākuḥ śreṣṭhadāyādo madhyadeśamavāptavān |
vasiṣṭhavacanādāsītpratiṣṭhānaṃ mahātmanaḥ ||
5.36.d:
इक्ष्वाकुः श्रेष्ठदायादो मध्यदेशमवाप्तवान् ।
वसिष्ठवचनादासीत्प्रतिष्ठानं महात्मनः ॥
5.36.m: Ikṣvāku, the eldest heir, obtained the middle region. / Pratiṣṭhāna belonged to the great-souled one by the word of Vasiṣṭha.

5.36.s:
pratiṣṭhāṃ dharmarājyasya sudyumno'tha tato dadau |
tatpurūravase prādād rājyaṃ prāpya mahāyaśāḥ ||
5.36.d:
प्रतिष्ठां धर्मराज्यस्य सुद्युम्नोऽथ ततो ददौ ।
तत्पुरूरवसे प्रादाद् राज्यं प्राप्य महायशाः ॥
5.36.m: Then Sudyumna gave stability to the righteous kingdom; / having attained the kingdom, the highly renowned one gave it to Purūravas.

5.36.s:
mānavo yo muniśreṣṭhāḥ strīpuṃsorlakṣaṇaḥ prabhuḥ |
nariṣyantācchakāḥ putrā nabhagasya suto'bhavat ||
5.36.d:
मानवो यो मुनिश्रेष्ठाः स्त्रीपुंसोर्लक्षणः प्रभुः ।
नरिष्यन्ताच्छकाः पुत्रा नभगस्य सुतोऽभवत् ॥
5.36.m: The son of Manu who had the characteristics of both woman and man, O best of sages, was a ruler. / From Nariṣyanta came the Śakas; [Ambarīṣa] was the son of Nabhaga.

5.36.s:
ambarīṣastu bāhleyo bāhlakaṃ kṣetrāmāptavān |
śaryātermithunaṃ tvāsīdānarto nāma viśrutaḥ ||
5.36.d:
अम्बरीषस्तु बाह्लेयो बाह्लकं क्षेत्रामाप्तवान् ।
शर्यातेर्मिथुनं त्वासीदानर्तो नाम विश्रुतः ॥
5.36.m: Ambarīṣa Bāhleya obtained the territory of Bāhlaka. / Śaryāti had a pair of twins: the famous son named Ānarta,

5.36.s:
putraḥ sukanyā kanyā ca yā patnī cyavanasya hi |
ānartasya hi dāyādo raibhyo nāma sa raivataḥ ||
5.36.d:
पुत्रः सुकन्या कन्या च या पत्नी च्यवनस्य हि ।
आनर्तस्य हि दायादो रैभ्यो नाम स रैवतः ॥
5.36.m: and the daughter Sukanyā, who was indeed the wife of Cyavana. / The heir of Ānarta was Raibhya, also named Raivata,

5.36.s:
ānartaviṣaye yasya purī nāma kuśasthalī |
mahādivyā saptapurīmadhye yā saptamī matā ||
5.36.d:
आनर्तविषये यस्य पुरी नाम कुशस्थली ।
महादिव्या सप्तपुरीमध्ये या सप्तमी मता ॥
5.36.m: whose city in the territory of Ānarta was named Kuśasthalī, / highly celestial, considered the seventh among the seven cities.

5.36.s:
tasya putraśataṃ tvāsītkakudmī jyeṣṭha uttamaḥ |
tejasvī subalaḥ pāro dharmiṣṭho brahmapālakaḥ ||
5.36.d:
तस्य पुत्रशतं त्वासीत्ककुद्मी ज्येष्ठ उत्तमः ।
तेजस्वी सुबलः पारो धर्मिष्ठो ब्रह्मपालकः ॥
5.36.m: He had a hundred sons, of whom Kakudmin was the eldest and best, / radiant, mighty, excellent, most righteous, and a protector of Brahmā.

5.36.s:
kakudminastu sañjātā revatī nāma kanyakā |
mahālāvaṇyasaṃyuktā divyalakṣmīrivāparā ||
5.36.d:
ककुद्मिनस्तु सञ्जाता रेवती नाम कन्यका ।
महालावण्यसंयुक्ता दिव्यलक्ष्मीरिवापरा ॥
5.36.m: To Kakudmin was born a daughter named Revatī, / endowed with great beauty, like another divine Lakṣmī.

5.36.s:
praṣṭuṃ kanyāvaraṃ rājā kakudmī kanyayā saha |
brahmaloke vidheḥ samyaksarvādhīśo jagāma ha ||
5.36.d:
प्रष्टुं कन्यावरं राजा ककुद्मी कन्यया सह ।
ब्रह्मलोके विधेः सम्यक्सर्वाधीशो जगाम ह ॥
5.36.m: To ask about a suitable bridegroom for his daughter, King Kakudmin, the sovereign of all, / went with his daughter directly to the brahmaloka of the Creator.

5.36.s:
āvartamāne gāndharve sthito labdhakṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇam |
śuśrāva tatra gāndharvaṃ nartane brahmaṇo'ntike ||
5.36.d:
आवर्तमाने गान्धर्वे स्थितो लब्धक्षणः क्षणम् ।
शुश्राव तत्र गान्धर्वं नर्तने ब्रह्मणोऽन्तिके ॥
5.36.m: While a musical performance was in progress, finding an opportune moment, he stayed for an instant / and listened to the Gandharva music at the dance in the presence of Brahmā.

5.36.s:
muhūrtabhūtaṃ tatkāle gataṃ bahuyugaṃ tadā |
na kiñcid bubudhe rājā kakudmī munayaḥ sa tu ||
5.36.d:
मुहूर्तभूतं तत्काले गतं बहुयुगं तदा ।
न किञ्चिद् बुबुधे राजा ककुद्मी मुनयः स तु ॥
5.36.m: That which seemed a mere muhūrta then was in fact many ages that had passed; / yet the king, Kakudmin, understood nothing of it, O sages.

5.36.s:
tadāsau vidhimānamya svābhiprāyaṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ |
nyavedayadvinītātmā brahmaṇe paramātmane ||
5.36.d:
तदासौ विधिमानम्य स्वाभिप्रायं कृताञ्जलिः ।
न्यवेदयद्विनीतात्मा ब्रह्मणे परमात्मने ॥
5.36.m: Then, having bowed to the Creator with folded hands, with a humble mind, / he submitted his intention to Brahmā, the Supreme Self.

5.36.s:
tadabhiprāyamākarṇya sa prahasya prajāpatiḥ |
kakudminaṃ mahārājaṃ samābhāṣya samabravīt ||
5.36.d:
तदभिप्रायमाकर्ण्य स प्रहस्य प्रजापतिः ।
ककुद्मिनं महाराजं समाभाष्य समब्रवीत् ॥
5.36.m: Hearing his intention, Prajāpati laughed, / addressed King Kakudmin, and spoke to him:

5.36.s:
brahmovāca |
śṛṇu rājan raibhyasuta kakudmin pṛthivīpate |
madvacaḥ prītitaḥ satyaṃ pravakṣyāmi viśeṣataḥ ||
5.36.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ।
शृणु राजन् रैभ्यसुत ककुद्मिन् पृथिवीपते ।
मद्वचः प्रीतितः सत्यं प्रवक्ष्यामि विशेषतः ॥
5.36.m: Brahmā said: / 'Listen, O king, son of Raibhya, Kakudmin, ruler of the earth! / Out of affection, I will declare my true word to you in detail.

5.36.s:
kālena saṃhṛtāste vai varā ye te kṛtā hṛdi |
na tadgotraṃ hi tatrāsti kālaḥ sarvasya bhakṣakaḥ ||
5.36.d:
कालेन संहृतास्ते वै वरा ये ते कृता हृदि ।
न तद्गोत्रं हि तत्रास्ति कालः सर्वस्य भक्षकः ॥
5.36.m: Those bridegrooms whom you had in mind have indeed been carried away by Time. / Nor does their lineage remain there; Time is the devourer of all.

5.36.s:
tvatpuryapi hatā puṇyajanaiḥ sā rākṣasairnṛpa |
aṣṭāviṃśadvāpare'dya kṛṣṇena nirmitā punaḥ ||
5.36.d:
त्वत्पुर्यपि हता पुण्यजनैः सा राक्षसैर्नृप ।
अष्टाविंशद्वापरेऽद्य कृष्णेन निर्मिता पुनः ॥
5.36.m: Even your city, O king, was destroyed by rākṣasas known as Puṇyajanas. / Now, in the twenty-eighth Dvāpara, it has been rebuilt by Kṛṣṇa,

5.36.s:
kṛtā dvārāvatī nāmnā bahudvārā manoramā |
bhojavṛṣṇyandhakairguptā vāsudevapurogamaiḥ ||
5.36.d:
कृता द्वारावती नाम्ना बहुद्वारा मनोरमा ।
भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकैर्गुप्ता वासुदेवपुरोगमैः ॥
5.36.m: named Dvārāvatī, delightful with many gateways, / protected by Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas headed by Vāsudeva.

5.36.s:
tadgaccha tatra prītātmā vāsudevāya kanyakām |
baladevāya dehi tvamimāṃ svatanayāṃ nṛpa ||
5.36.d:
तद्गच्छ तत्र प्रीतात्मा वासुदेवाय कन्यकाम् ।
बलदेवाय देहि त्वमिमां स्वतनयां नृप ॥
5.36.m: Therefore go there with a glad heart, O king, / and bestow this daughter of yours, your own child, upon Baladeva, the brother of Vāsudeva.'

5.36.s:
sūta uvāca |
ityādiṣṭo nṛpo'yaṃ taṃ natvā tāṃ ca purīṃ gataḥ |
gatān bahūnyugān jñātvā vismitaḥ kanyayā yutaḥ ||
5.36.d:
सूत उवाच ।
इत्यादिष्टो नृपोऽयं तं नत्वा तां च पुरीं गतः ।
गतान् बहून्युगान् ज्ञात्वा विस्मितः कन्यया युतः ॥
5.36.m: Sūta said: / Thus instructed, the king bowed to him and went to that city; / realizing that many ages had passed, he was astonished, accompanied by his daughter.

5.36.s:
tatastu yuvatīṃ kanyāṃ tāṃ ca svāṃ suvidhānataḥ |
kṛṣṇabhrātre balāyāśu prādāttatra sa revatīm ||
5.36.d:
ततस्तु युवतीं कन्यां तां च स्वां सुविधानतः ।
कृष्णभ्रात्रे बलायाशु प्रादात्तत्र स रेवतीम् ॥
5.36.m: Then, according to proper rite, he immediately gave that maiden daughter of his, / Revatī, to Bala, the brother of Kṛṣṇa, in that city.

5.36.s:
tato jagāma śikharaṃ merordivyaṃ mahāprabhuḥ |
śivamārādhayāmāsa sa nṛpastapasi sthitaḥ ||
5.36.d:
ततो जगाम शिखरं मेरोर्दिव्यं महाप्रभुः ।
शिवमाराधयामास स नृपस्तपसि स्थितः ॥
5.36.m: Then that great lord went to the divine peak of Mount Meru; / established in austerity, the king worshipped Śiva.

5.36.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ |
tatra sthito bahuyugaṃ brahmaloke sa revataḥ |
yuvaivāgānmartyalokametannaḥ saṃśayo mahān ||
5.36.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः ।
तत्र स्थितो बहुयुगं ब्रह्मलोके स रेवतः ।
युवैवागान्मर्त्यलोकमेतन्नः संशयो महान् ॥
5.36.m: The sages said: / 'Remaining there in the brahmaloka for many ages, that Raivata / returned to the mortal world still youthful—this is our great doubt!'

5.36.s:
sūta uvāca |
na jarā kṣutpipāsā vā vikārāstatra santi vai |
apamṛtyurna keṣāñcinmunayo brahmaṇoṃ'tike ||
5.36.d:
सूत उवाच ।
न जरा क्षुत्पिपासा वा विकारास्तत्र सन्ति वै ।
अपमृत्युर्न केषाञ्चिन्मुनयो ब्रह्मणोंऽतिके ॥
5.36.m: Sūta said: / 'There is no old age, hunger, thirst, or afflictions there; / nor is there untimely death for anyone in the presence of Brahmā, O sages.

5.36.s:
ato na rājā samprāpa jarāṃ mṛtyuṃ ca sā sutā |
sa yuvaivāgatastatra sammantrya tanayāvaram ||
5.36.d:
अतो न राजा सम्प्राप जरां मृत्युं च सा सुता ।
स युवैवागतस्तत्र सम्मन्त्र्य तनयावरम् ॥
5.36.m: Therefore the king did not suffer old age or death, nor did his daughter. / He returned still young, having consulted regarding a bridegroom for his daughter.

5.36.s:
gatvā dvārāvatīṃ divyāṃ purīṃ kṛṣṇavinirmitām |
vivāhaṃ kārayāmāsa kanyāyāḥ sa balena hi ||
5.36.d:
गत्वा द्वारावतीं दिव्यां पुरीं कृष्णविनिर्मिताम् ।
विवाहं कारयामास कन्यायाः स बलेन हि ॥
5.36.m: Having gone to the divine city of Dvārāvatī built by Kṛṣṇa, / he celebrated the marriage of his daughter with Bala.

5.36.s:
tasya putraśataṃ tvāsīddhārmikasya mahāprabhoḥ |
kṛṣṇasyāpi sutā jātā bahustrībhyo'mitāstataḥ ||
5.36.d:
तस्य पुत्रशतं त्वासीद्धार्मिकस्य महाप्रभोः ।
कृष्णस्यापि सुता जाता बहुस्त्रीभ्योऽमितास्ततः ॥
5.36.m: That righteous, mighty lord had a hundred sons; / and to Kṛṣṇa too, immeasurable sons were born from many wives.

5.36.s:
anvavāyo mahāṃstatra dvayorapi mahātmanoḥ |
kṣatriyā dikṣu sarvāsu gatā hṛṣṭāḥ sudhārmikāḥ ||
5.36.d:
अन्ववायो महांस्तत्र द्वयोरपि महात्मनोः ।
क्षत्रिया दिक्षु सर्वासु गता हृष्टाः सुधार्मिकाः ॥
5.36.m: The lineage of both those great-souled ones was great; / the kṣatriyas, very righteous, went forth happily in all directions.

5.36.s:
iti prokto hi śaryātervaṃśo'nyeṣāṃ vadāmyaham |
mānavānāṃ hi saṅkṣepācchṛṇutādarato dvijāḥ ||
5.36.d:
इति प्रोक्तो हि शर्यातेर्वंशोऽन्येषां वदाम्यहम् ।
मानवानां हि सङ्क्षेपाच्छृणुतादरतो द्विजाः ॥
5.36.m: Thus the lineage of Śaryāti has been related; I shall speak of the others / descended from Manu in brief. Listen with reverence, O twice-born!

5.36.s:
nābhāgo diṣṭaputro'bhūtsa tu brāhmaṇatāṃ gataḥ |
svakṣatravaṃśaṃ saṃsthāpya brahmakarmabhirāvṛtaḥ ||
5.36.d:
नाभागो दिष्टपुत्रोऽभूत्स तु ब्राह्मणतां गतः ।
स्वक्षत्रवंशं संस्थाप्य ब्रह्मकर्मभिरावृतः ॥
5.36.m: Nābhāga was the son of Diṣṭa; he attained the state of a brāhmaṇa, / having established his own kṣatriya line and devoted himself to Vedic rites.

5.36.s:
dhṛṣṭāddhārṣṭamabhūtkṣatraṃ brahmabhūyaṃ gataṃ kṣitau |
karūṣasya tu kārūṣāḥ kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ ||
5.36.d:
धृष्टाद्धार्ष्टमभूत्क्षत्रं ब्रह्मभूयं गतं क्षितौ ।
करूषस्य तु कारूषाः क्षत्रिया युद्धदुर्मदाः ॥
5.36.m: From Dhṛṣṭa sprang the Dhārṣṭa kṣatriyas, who attained the state of Brahmā on earth; / and Karūṣa’s descendants were the Kārūṣas, kṣatriyas fierce in battle.

5.36.s:
nṛgo yo manuputrastu mahādātā viśeṣataḥ |
nānāvasūnāṃ suprītyā viprebhyaśca gavāṃ tathā ||
5.36.d:
नृगो यो मनुपुत्रस्तु महादाता विशेषतः ।
नानावसूनां सुप्रीत्या विप्रेभ्यश्च गवां तथा ॥
5.36.m: Nṛga, who was a son of Manu, was especially a great giver / of various wealth and cows with great joy to brāhmaṇas.

5.36.s:
godānavyatyayādyastu svakubuddhyā svapāpataḥ |
kṛkalāsatvamāpannaḥ śrīkṛṣṇena samuddhṛtaḥ ||
5.36.d:
गोदानव्यत्ययाद्यस्तु स्वकुबुद्ध्या स्वपापतः ।
कृकलासत्वमापन्नः श्रीकृष्णेन समुद्धृतः ॥
5.36.m: Owing to an error in the gift of a cow, through his own bad judgment and sin, / he fell into the state of a chameleon and was delivered by Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

5.36.s:
tasyaiko'bhūtsutaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ prayātirdharmavittathā |
iti śrutaṃ mayā vyāsāttatproktaṃ hi samāsataḥ ||
5.36.d:
तस्यैकोऽभूत्सुतः श्रेष्ठः प्रयातिर्धर्मवित्तथा ।
इति श्रुतं मया व्यासात्तत्प्रोक्तं हि समासतः ॥
5.36.m: He had an excellent son named Prayāti, who knew the law; / thus I have heard it from Vyāsa, and it has been told in brief.

5.36.s:
vṛṣaghnastu manoḥ putro gopālo guruṇā kṛtaḥ |
pālayāmāsa gā yatto rātryāṃ vīrāsanavrataḥ ||
5.36.d:
वृषघ्नस्तु मनोः पुत्रो गोपालो गुरुणा कृतः ।
पालयामास गा यत्तो रात्र्यां वीरासनव्रतः ॥
5.36.m: Vṛṣaghna, the son of Manu, was made a cowherd by his preceptor; / observing the vow of the hero's posture, he diligently protected the cows at night.

5.36.s:
sa ekadāgataṃ goṣṭhe vyāghraṃ gā hiṃsituṃ balī |
śrutvā gokrandanaṃ buddho hantuṃ taṃ khaḍgadhṛgyayau ||
5.36.d:
स एकदागतं गोष्ठे व्याघ्रं गा हिंसितुं बली ।
श्रुत्वा गोक्रन्दनं बुद्धो हन्तुं तं खड्गधृग्ययौ ॥
5.36.m: Once, a tiger came into the cow-pen to kill cows; / hearing the bellowing of a cow, the strong man woke up and went, sword in hand, to kill it.

5.36.s:
ajānannahanadbabhroḥ śiraḥ śārdūlaśaṅkayā |
niścakrāma sabhīrvyāghro dṛṣṭvā taṃ khaḍginaṃ prabhum ||
5.36.d:
अजानन्नहनद्बभ्रोः शिरः शार्दूलशङ्कया ।
निश्चक्राम सभीर्व्याघ्रो दृष्ट्वा तं खड्गिनं प्रभुम् ॥
5.36.m: Unknowingly, suspecting it was a tiger, he struck the head of a tawny cow; / seeing the lord with a sword, the terrified tiger slipped away.

5.36.s:
manyamāno hataṃ vyāghraṃ svasthānaṃ sa jagāma ha |
rātryāṃ tasyāṃ bhramāpanno varṣavātavinaṣṭadhīḥ ||
5.36.d:
मन्यमानो हतं व्याघ्रं स्वस्थानं स जगाम ह ।
रात्र्यां तस्यां भ्रमापन्नो वर्षवातविनष्टधीः ॥
5.36.m: Thinking the tiger was slain, he returned to his place; / on that night he was bewildered, his mind confounded by the wind and rain.

5.36.s:
vyuṣṭāyāṃ niśi cotthāya prage tatra gato hi saḥ |
adrākṣītsa hatāṃ babhruṃ na vyāghraṃ duḥkhito'bhavat ||
5.36.d:
व्युष्टायां निशि चोत्थाय प्रगे तत्र गतो हि सः ।
अद्राक्षीत्स हतां बभ्रुं न व्याघ्रं दुःखितोऽभवत् ॥
5.36.m: When night had dawned, he arose and went there early in the morning; / he saw the tawny cow slain, not the tiger, and was filled with sorrow.

5.36.s:
śrutvā tadvṛttamājñāya taṃ śaśāpa kṛtāgasam |
akāmato vicāryeti śūdro bhava na kṣatriyaḥ ||
5.36.d:
श्रुत्वा तद्वृत्तमाज्ञाय तं शशाप कृतागसम् ।
अकामतो विचार्येति शूद्रो भव न क्षत्रियः ॥
5.36.m: Hearing of that incident and learning of it, [his preceptor] cursed him who had committed the sin: / 'Though it was done unintentionally, having considered this: become a śūdra, not a kṣatriya!'

5.36.s:
evaṃ śaptastu guruṇā kulācāryeṇa kopataḥ |
niḥsṛtaśca pṛṣadhrastu jagāma vipinaṃ mahat ||
5.36.d:
एवं शप्तस्तु गुरुणा कुलाचार्येण कोपतः ।
निःसृतश्च पृषध्रस्तु जगाम विपिनं महत् ॥
5.36.m: Thus cursed in anger by his preceptor, the family teacher, / Pṛṣadhra departed and went into the vast forest.

5.36.s:
nirviṇṇaḥ sa tu kaṣṭena virakto'bhūtsa yogavān |
vanāgnau dagdhadehaśca jagāma paramāṃ gatim ||
5.36.d:
निर्विण्णः स तु कष्टेन विरक्तोऽभूत्स योगवान् ।
वनाग्नौ दग्धदेहश्च जगाम परमां गतिम् ॥
5.36.m: Dejected through suffering, he became detached and practiced yoga; / with his body consumed in a forest fire, he attained the supreme state.

5.36.s:
kaviḥ putro manoḥ prājñaḥ śivānugrahato'bhavat |
iha bhuktvā sukhaṃ divyaṃ muktiṃ prāpa sudurlabhām ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.36.d:
कविः पुत्रो मनोः प्राज्ञः शिवानुग्रहतोऽभवत् ।
इह भुक्त्वा सुखं दिव्यं मुक्तिं प्राप सुदुर्लभाम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.36.m:
Kavi, the son of Manu, was wise by the grace of Śiva; / having enjoyed divine happiness here, he attained rare liberation.

Homage to the auspicious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.37.s:
sūta uvāca |
pūrvatastu manorjajñe ikṣvākurghrāṇataḥ sutaḥ |
tasya putraśataṃ tvāsīdikṣvākorbhūridakṣiṇam ||
5.37.d:
सूत उवाच ।
पूर्वतस्तु मनोर्जज्ञे इक्ष्वाकुर्घ्राणतः सुतः ।
तस्य पुत्रशतं त्वासीदिक्ष्वाकोर्भूरिदक्षिणम् ॥
5.37.m: Sūta said: / Formerly, Ikṣvāku was born as a son from the nostrils of Manu; / that Ikṣvāku had a hundred sons who gave abundant sacrificial fees.

5.37.s:
teṣāṃ purastādabhavannāryāvarte nṛpā dvijāḥ |
teṣāṃ vikukṣirjyeṣṭhastu so'yodhyāyāṃ nṛpo'bhavat ||
5.37.d:
तेषां पुरस्तादभवन्नार्यावर्ते नृपा द्विजाः ।
तेषां विकुक्षिर्ज्येष्ठस्तु सोऽयोध्यायां नृपोऽभवत् ॥
5.37.m: In front of them were kings in Āryāvarta, O twice-born! / Vikukṣi was the eldest of them, and he became the king in Ayodhyā.

5.37.s:
tatkarma śṛṇu tatprītyā yajjātaṃ vaṃśato vidheḥ |
śrāddhakarmaṇi coddiṣṭo hyakṛte śrāddhakarmaṇi ||
5.37.d:
तत्कर्म शृणु तत्प्रीत्या यज्जातं वंशतो विधेः ।
श्राद्धकर्मणि चोद्दिष्टो ह्यकृते श्राद्धकर्मणि ॥
5.37.m: Listen with affection to his deed that arose in the lineage of the Creator: / appointed for the śrāddha rite, before the śrāddha rite was performed,

5.37.s:
bhakṣayitvā śaśaṃ śīghraṃ śaśādatvamato gataḥ |
ikṣvākuṇā parityaktaḥ śaśādo vanamāviśat ||
5.37.d:
भक्षयित्वा शशं शीघ्रं शशादत्वमतो गतः ।
इक्ष्वाकुणा परित्यक्तः शशादो वनमाविशत् ॥
5.37.m: he quickly ate a hare, and so he was called Śaśāda; / abandoned by Ikṣvāku, Śaśāda entered the forest.

5.37.s:
ikṣvākau saṃsthite rājā vasiṣṭhavacanādabhūt |
śakunipramukhāstasya putrāḥ pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ ||
5.37.d:
इक्ष्वाकौ संस्थिते राजा वसिष्ठवचनादभूत् ।
शकुनिप्रमुखास्तस्य पुत्राः पञ्चदश स्मृताः ॥
5.37.m: When Ikṣvāku passed away, he became king by the word of Vasiṣṭha; / fifteen sons of his are remembered, headed by Śakuni,

5.37.s:
uttarāpathadeśasya rakṣitāro mahīkṣitaḥ |
ayodhasya tu dāyādaḥ kakutstho nāma vīryavān ||
5.37.d:
उत्तरापथदेशस्य रक्षितारो महीक्षितः ।
अयोधस्य तु दायादः ककुत्स्थो नाम वीर्यवान् ॥
5.37.m: rulers of the earth who protected the northern region. / The son of Ayodha was the heroic Kakutstha;

5.37.s:
arinābhaḥ kakutsthasya pṛthuretasya vai sutaḥ |
viṣṭarāśvaḥ pṛthoḥ putrastasmādindraḥ prajāpatiḥ ||
5.37.d:
अरिनाभः ककुत्स्थस्य पृथुरेतस्य वै सुतः ।
विष्टराश्वः पृथोः पुत्रस्तस्मादिन्द्रः प्रजापतिः ॥
5.37.m: Arinābha was Kakutstha’s son; Pṛthu was his son; / Viṣṭarāśva was the son of Pṛthu; from him came Indra Prajāpati.

5.37.s:
indrasya yuvanāśvastu śrāvastasya prajāpatiḥ |
jajñe śrāvastakaḥ prājñaḥ śrāvastī yena nirmitā |
śrāvastasya tu dāyādo bṛhadaśvo mahāyaśāḥ ||
5.37.d:
इन्द्रस्य युवनाश्वस्तु श्रावस्तस्य प्रजापतिः ।
जज्ञे श्रावस्तकः प्राज्ञः श्रावस्ती येन निर्मिता ।
श्रावस्तस्य तु दायादो बृहदश्वो महायशाः ॥
5.37.m: Indra’s son was Yuvanāśva; Śrāvasta was his son, the progenitor; / the wise Śrāvastaka was born, by whom Śrāvastī was founded; / and the heir of Śrāvasta was the highly renowned Bṛhadaśva.

5.37.s:
yuvanāśvaḥ sutastasya kuvalāśvaśca tatsutaḥ |
sa hi dhundhuvadhādbhūto dhundhumāro nṛpottamaḥ ||
5.37.d:
युवनाश्वः सुतस्तस्य कुवलाश्वश्च तत्सुतः ।
स हि धुन्धुवधाद्भूतो धुन्धुमारो नृपोत्तमः ॥
5.37.m: His son was Yuvanāśva, and his son was Kuvalāśva. / From slaying Dhundhu, he became Dhundhumāra, the best of kings.

5.37.s:
kuvalāśvasya putrāṇāṃ śatamuttamadhanvinām |
babhūvātha pitā rājye kuvalāśvaṃ nyayojayat ||
5.37.d:
कुवलाश्वस्य पुत्राणां शतमुत्तमधन्विनाम् ।
बभूवाथ पिता राज्ये कुवलाश्वं न्ययोजयत् ॥
5.37.m: Kuvalāśva had a hundred sons, excellent archers. / Then the father installed Kuvalāśva on the throne.

5.37.s:
putrasaṅkrāmitaśrīko vanaṃ rājā samāviśat |
tamuttaṅko'tha rājarṣiḥ prayāntaṃ pratyavārayat ||
5.37.d:
पुत्रसङ्क्रामितश्रीको वनं राजा समाविशत् ।
तमुत्तङ्कोऽथ राजर्षिः प्रयान्तं प्रत्यवारयत् ॥
5.37.m: Having transferred his royal fortune to his son, the king entered the forest. / As he was departing, the royal sage Uttaṅka stopped him.

5.37.s:
uttaṅka uvāca |
bhavatā rakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ pṛthivyā dharmataḥ śṛṇu |
tvayā hi pṛthivī rājan rakṣyamāṇā mahātmanā ||
5.37.d:
उत्तङ्क उवाच ।
भवता रक्षणं कार्यं पृथिव्या धर्मतः शृणु ।
त्वया हि पृथिवी राजन् रक्ष्यमाणा महात्मना ॥
5.37.m: Uttaṅka said: / “The earth must be protected by you according to dharma; listen! / For when the earth is protected by you, the great-souled one, O king,

5.37.s:
bhaviṣyati nirudvignā nāraṇyaṃ gantumarhasi |
mamāśramasamīpe tu sameṣu marudhanvasu ||
5.37.d:
भविष्यति निरुद्विग्ना नारण्यं गन्तुमर्हसि ।
ममाश्रमसमीपे तु समेषु मरुधन्वसु ॥
5.37.m: she will be free from anxiety; you ought not to go to the forest. / Near my hermitage, on level desert sands

5.37.s:
samudravālukāpūrṇe dānavo baladarpitaḥ |
devatānāmavadhyo hi mahākāyo mahābalaḥ ||
5.37.d:
समुद्रवालुकापूर्णे दानवो बलदर्पितः ।
देवतानामवध्यो हि महाकायो महाबलः ॥
5.37.m: filled with sea sand, there is a Dānava proud of his strength. / He is invulnerable to the gods, possessing a huge body and great might.

5.37.s:
antarbhūmigatastatra vālukāntarhitaḥ sthitaḥ |
rākṣasasya madhoḥ putro dhundhunāmā sudāruṇaḥ ||
5.37.d:
अन्तर्भूमिगतस्तत्र वालुकान्तर्हितः स्थितः ।
राक्षसस्य मधोः पुत्रो धुन्धुनामा सुदारुणः ॥
5.37.m: Dwelling underground there, concealed in the sand, / resides the son of the Rākṣasa Madhu, named Dhundhu, extremely dreadful.

5.37.s:
śete lokavināśāya tapa āsthāya dāruṇam |
saṃvatsarasya paryante sa niśvāsaṃ vimuñcati ||
5.37.d:
शेते लोकविनाशाय तप आस्थाय दारुणम् ।
संवत्सरस्य पर्यन्ते स निश्वासं विमुञ्चति ॥
5.37.m: He lies there to destroy the worlds, undertaking terrible austerity. / At the end of every year he exhales his breath.

5.37.s:
yadā tadā bhūścalati saśailavanakānanā |
savisphuliṅgaṃ sāṅgāraṃ sadhūmamatidāruṇam ||
5.37.d:
यदा तदा भूश्चलति सशैलवनकानना ।
सविस्फुलिङ्गं साङ्गारं सधूममतिदारुणम् ॥
5.37.m: When [he does] that, the earth trembles with its mountains, forests, and woods, / with sparks, embers, and smoke, exceedingly dreadful.

5.37.s:
tena rāyanna śaknomi tasminn sthātuṃ sva āśrame |
taṃ māraya mahābāho lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā ||
5.37.d:
तेन रायन्न शक्नोमि तस्मिन्न् स्थातुं स्व आश्रमे ।
तं मारय महाबाहो लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
5.37.m: Because of that, O king, I cannot remain in my own hermitage. / Slay him, O mighty-armed one, desiring the welfare of the worlds!

5.37.s:
lokāḥ svasthā bhavantvadya tasmin vinihate tvayā |
tvaṃ hi tasya vadhāyaiva samarthaḥ pṛthivīpate ||
5.37.d:
लोकाः स्वस्था भवन्त्वद्य तस्मिन् विनिहते त्वया ।
त्वं हि तस्य वधायैव समर्थः पृथिवीपते ॥
5.37.m: Let the worlds become tranquil today once he is slain by you. / For you alone are capable of slaying him, O lord of the earth!

5.37.s:
viṣṇunā ca varo datto mahya pūrvayuge'nagha |
tejasā svena te viṣṇusteja āpyāyayiṣyati ||
5.37.d:
विष्णुना च वरो दत्तो मह्य पूर्वयुगेऽनघ ।
तेजसा स्वेन ते विष्णुस्तेज आप्याययिष्यति ॥
5.37.m: And a boon was granted to me by Viṣṇu in a previous age, O sinless one: / Viṣṇu will augment your splendour with his own splendour.

5.37.s:
pālane hi mahān dharmaḥ prajānāmiha dṛśyate |
na tathā dṛśyate'raṇye mā te'bhūd buddhirīdṛśī ||
5.37.d:
पालने हि महान् धर्मः प्रजानामिह दृश्यते ।
न तथा दृश्यतेऽरण्ये मा तेऽभूद् बुद्धिरीदृशी ॥
5.37.m: For great dharma is seen in this world in protecting the subjects; / it is not seen to be so in the forest; let such a notion not be yours!

5.37.s:
īdṛśo na hi rājendra kvaciddharmaḥ pravidyate |
prajānāṃ pālane yādṛk purā rājarṣibhiḥ kṛtaḥ ||
5.37.d:
ईदृशो न हि राजेन्द्र क्वचिद्धर्मः प्रविद्यते ।
प्रजानां पालने यादृक् पुरा राजर्षिभिः कृतः ॥
5.37.m: Indeed, O king of kings, no such dharma exists anywhere / as that practiced formerly by royal sages in protecting the subjects.”

5.37.s:
sa evamukto rājarṣiruttaṅkena mahātmanā |
kuvalāśvaṃ sutaṃ prādāttasmai dhundhunivāraṇe ||
5.37.d:
स एवमुक्तो राजर्षिरुत्तङ्केन महात्मना ।
कुवलाश्वं सुतं प्रादात्तस्मै धुन्धुनिवारणे ॥
5.37.m: Thus addressed by the great-souled Uttaṅka, that royal sage / gave him his son Kuvalāśva for restraining Dhundhu:

5.37.s:
bhagavannyastaśastro'hamayaṃ tu tanayo mama |
bhaviṣyati dvijaśreṣṭha dhundhumāro na saṃśayaḥ ||
5.37.d:
भगवन्न्यस्तशस्त्रोऽहमयं तु तनयो मम ।
भविष्यति द्विजश्रेष्ठ धुन्धुमारो न संशयः ॥
5.37.m: “O venerable one, I have laid down my weapons, but this son of mine / will become Dhundhumāra, O best of the twice-born, without doubt.”

5.37.s:
ityuktvā putramādiśya yayau sa tapase nṛpaḥ |
kuvalāśvaśca sottaṅko yayau dhundhuvinigrahe ||
5.37.d:
इत्युक्त्वा पुत्रमादिश्य ययौ स तपसे नृपः ।
कुवलाश्वश्च सोत्तङ्को ययौ धुन्धुविनिग्रहे ॥
5.37.m: Having said this and instructed his son, the king went away for austerity, / and Kuvalāśva along with Uttaṅka departed to vanquish Dhundhu.

5.37.s:
tamāviśattadā viṣṇurbhagavāṃstejasā prabhuḥ |
uttaṅkasya niyogādvai lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā ||
5.37.d:
तमाविशत्तदा विष्णुर्भगवांस्तेजसा प्रभुः ।
उत्तङ्कस्य नियोगाद्वै लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
5.37.m: Then the lord, venerable Viṣṇu, entered him with his splendour / at Uttaṅka's command, desiring the welfare of the worlds.

5.37.s:
tasminprayāte durdharṣe divi śabdo mahānabhūt |
eṣa śrīmānnṛpasuto dhundhumāro bhaviṣyati ||
5.37.d:
तस्मिन्प्रयाते दुर्धर्षे दिवि शब्दो महानभूत् ।
एष श्रीमान्नृपसुतो धुन्धुमारो भविष्यति ॥
5.37.m: As that invincible one set out, a great sound arose in heaven: / “This glorious prince will become Dhundhumāra!”

5.37.s:
divyairmālyaiśca taṃ devāḥ samantātsamavārayan |
praśaṃsāṃ cakrire tasya jaya jīveti vādinaḥ ||
5.37.d:
दिव्यैर्माल्यैश्च तं देवाः समन्तात्समवारयन् ।
प्रशंसां चक्रिरे तस्य जय जीवेति वादिनः ॥
5.37.m: And the gods showered him all around with celestial garlands, / and praised him, saying, “Be victorious! Live long!”

5.37.s:
sa gatvā jayatāṃ śreṣṭhastanayaiḥ saha pārthivaḥ |
samudraṃ khanayāmāsa vālukārṇavamadhyataḥ ||
5.37.d:
स गत्वा जयतां श्रेष्ठस्तनयैः सह पार्थिवः ।
समुद्रं खनयामास वालुकार्णवमध्यतः ॥
5.37.m: Having gone, that king, the best among victors, together with his sons, / caused the sea of sand to be excavated from the middle.

5.37.s:
nārāyaṇasya viprarṣestejasāpyāyitastu saḥ |
babhūva sumahātejā bhūyo balasamanvitaḥ ||
5.37.d:
नारायणस्य विप्रर्षेस्तेजसाप्यायितस्तु सः ।
बभूव सुमहातेजा भूयो बलसमन्वितः ॥
5.37.m: Augmented by the splendour of Nārāyaṇa, the sage among the twice-born, / he became endowed with immense splendour and exceedingly great strength.

5.37.s:
tasya putraiḥ khanadbhistu vālukāntargatastu saḥ |
dhundhurāsādito brahman diśamāśritya paści mām ||
5.37.d:
तस्य पुत्रैः खनद्भिस्तु वालुकान्तर्गतस्तु सः ।
धुन्धुरासादितो ब्रह्मन् दिशमाश्रित्य पश्चि माम् ॥
5.37.m: As his sons were digging, that Dhundhu lying within the sand / was reached, O brahmin, having taken refuge in the western direction.

5.37.s:
mukhajenāgninā krodhāllokān saṃvartayanniva |
vāri susrāva vegena vidhoḥ kadhirivodaye ||
5.37.d:
मुखजेनाग्निना क्रोधाल्लोकान् संवर्तयन्निव ।
वारि सुस्राव वेगेन विधोः कधिरिवोदये ॥
5.37.m: With fire issuing from his mouth in anger, as if dissolving the worlds, / he violently discharged water, as the moon [draws] the tide at its rising.

5.37.s:
tato'nalairabhihataṃ dagdhaṃ putraśataṃ hi tat |
traya evāvaśiṣṭāśca teṣu madhye munīśvara ||
5.37.d:
ततोऽनलैरभिहतं दग्धं पुत्रशतं हि तत् ।
त्रय एवावशिष्टाश्च तेषु मध्ये मुनीश्वर ॥
5.37.m: Then struck by the fires, that hundred sons was consumed indeed; / only three remained among them, O lord of sages.

5.37.s:
tataḥ sa rājā viprendra rākṣasaṃ taṃ mahābalam |
āsasāda mahātejā dhundhuṃ vipravināśanam ||
5.37.d:
ततः स राजा विप्रेन्द्र राक्षसं तं महाबलम् ।
आससाद महातेजा धुन्धुं विप्रविनाशनम् ॥
5.37.m: Then that king of great splendour, O foremost of the twice-born, / approached that mighty Rākṣasa Dhundhu, the destroyer of brahmins.

5.37.s:
tasya vārimayaṃ vegamāpīya sa narādhipaḥ |
vahnibāṇena vahniṃ tu śamayāmāsa vāriṇā ||
5.37.d:
तस्य वारिमयं वेगमापीय स नराधिपः ।
वह्निबाणेन वह्निं तु शमयामास वारिणा ॥
5.37.m: Drinking up his watery surge, the lord of men / extinguished the fire with water, and [subdued] the fire with an arrow.

5.37.s:
taṃ nihatya mahākāyaṃ balenodakarākṣasam |
uttaṅkasyekṣayāmāsa kṛtaṃ karma narādhipaḥ ||
5.37.d:
तं निहत्य महाकायं बलेनोदकराक्षसम् ।
उत्तङ्कस्येक्षयामास कृतं कर्म नराधिपः ॥
5.37.m: Having slain with his might that huge-bodied water-demon, / the lord of men showed Uttaṅka the deed that had been accomplished.

5.37.s:
uttaṅkastu varaṃ prādāttasmai rājñe mahāmune |
adadaccākṣayaṃ vittaṃ śatrubhiścāparājayam ||
5.37.d:
उत्तङ्कस्तु वरं प्रादात्तस्मै राज्ञे महामुने ।
अददच्चाक्षयं वित्तं शत्रुभिश्चापराजयम् ॥
5.37.m: Then Uttaṅka granted a boon to that king, O great sage, / and bestowed inexhaustible wealth and invincibility against enemies,

5.37.s:
dharme matiṃ ca satataṃ svarge vāsaṃ tathākṣayam |
putrāṇāṃ cākṣayaṃ lokaṃ rakṣasā ye tu saṃhatāḥ ||
5.37.d:
धर्मे मतिं च सततं स्वर्गे वासं तथाक्षयम् ।
पुत्राणां चाक्षयं लोकं रक्षसा ये तु संहताः ॥
5.37.m: a mind ever fixed on dharma, and imperishable residence in heaven, / as well as an imperishable realm for the sons who had been killed by the Rākṣasa.

5.37.s:
tasya putrāstrayaḥ śiṣṭāḥ dṛḍhāśvaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate |
haṃsāśvakapilāśvau ca kumārau tatkanīyasau ||
5.37.d:
तस्य पुत्रास्त्रयः शिष्टाः दृढाश्वः श्रेष्ठ उच्यते ।
हंसाश्वकपिलाश्वौ च कुमारौ तत्कनीयसौ ॥
5.37.m: Three sons of his remained: Dṛḍhāśva is said to be the eldest, / and Haṃsāśva and Kapilāśva were the two younger princes.

5.37.s:
dhaundhumārirdṛḍhāśvo yo haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ |
haryaśvasya nikumbho'bhūtputro dharmarataḥ sadā ||
5.37.d:
धौन्धुमारिर्दृढाश्वो यो हर्यश्वस्तस्य चात्मजः ।
हर्यश्वस्य निकुम्भोऽभूत्पुत्रो धर्मरतः सदा ॥
5.37.m: The son of Dhundhumāra was Dṛḍhāśva, and his son was Haryaśva; / Haryaśva had a son named Nikumbha, ever devoted to dharma.

5.37.s:
saṃhatāśvo nikumbhasya putro raṇaviśāradaḥ |
akṣāśvaśca kṛtāśvaśca saṃhatāśvasutau dvijāḥ ||
5.37.d:
संहताश्वो निकुम्भस्य पुत्रो रणविशारदः ।
अक्षाश्वश्च कृताश्वश्च संहताश्वसुतौ द्विजाः ॥
5.37.m: Nikumbha’s son was Saṃhatāśva, skilled in battle; / Akṣāśva and Kṛtāśva were the two sons of Saṃhatāśva, O twice-born.

5.37.s:
tasya haimavatī bhāryā satāṃ mānyā dṛṣadvatī |
vikhyātā triṣu lokeṣu putrastasyāḥ prasenajit ||
5.37.d:
तस्य हैमवती भार्या सतां मान्या दृषद्वती ।
विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु पुत्रस्तस्याः प्रसेनजित् ॥
5.37.m: His wife was Haimavatī Dṛṣadvatī, honoured by the virtuous, / renowned in the three worlds; her son was Prasenajit.

5.37.s:
lebhe prasenajidbhāryāṃ gaurīṃ nāma pativratām |
abhiśaptā tu sā bhartrā nadī sā bāhudā kṛtā ||
5.37.d:
लेभे प्रसेनजिद्भार्यां गौरीं नाम पतिव्रताम् ।
अभिशप्ता तु सा भर्त्रा नदी सा बाहुदा कृता ॥
5.37.m: Prasenajit took as wife Gaurī by name, devoted to her husband; / but cursed by her husband, she was turned into the Bāhudā River.

5.37.s:
tasya putro mahānāsīdyuvanāśvo mahīpatiḥ |
māndhātā yuvanāśvasya triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ ||
5.37.d:
तस्य पुत्रो महानासीद्युवनाश्वो महीपतिः ।
मान्धाता युवनाश्वस्य त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः ॥
5.37.m: His son was the great Yuvanāśva, lord of the earth; / Yuvanāśva's [son] was Māndhātṛ, renowned in the three worlds.

5.37.s:
tasya caitrarathī bhāryā śaśabindusutā'bhavat |
pativratā ca jyeṣṭhā ca bhrātṝṇāmayutasya sā ||
5.37.d:
तस्य चैत्ररथी भार्या शशबिन्दुसुताऽभवत् ।
पतिव्रता च ज्येष्ठा च भ्रातॄणामयुतस्य सा ॥
5.37.m: His wife was Caitrarathī, the daughter of Śaśabindu, / devoted to her husband, and the eldest of ten thousand brothers.

5.37.s:
tasyāmutpādayāmāsa māndhātā dvau sutau tadā |
purukutsaṃ ca dharmajñaṃ mucukundaṃ ca dhārmikam ||
5.37.d:
तस्यामुत्पादयामास मान्धाता द्वौ सुतौ तदा ।
पुरुकुत्सं च धर्मज्ञं मुचुकुन्दं च धार्मिकम् ॥
5.37.m: Upon her Māndhātṛ then begot two sons: / Purukutsa, knower of dharma, and the righteous Mucukunda.

5.37.s:
purukutsasutastvāsīdvidvāṃstrayyāruṇiḥ kaviḥ |
tasya satyavrato nāma kumāro'bhūnmahābalī ||
5.37.d:
पुरुकुत्ससुतस्त्वासीद्विद्वांस्त्रय्यारुणिः कविः ।
तस्य सत्यव्रतो नाम कुमारोऽभून्महाबली ॥
5.37.m: Purukutsa's son was Trayyāruṇi, wise and a poet; / his prince was named Satyavrata, endowed with great might.

5.37.s:
pāṇigrahaṇamantrāṇāṃ vighraṃ cakre mahātmabhiḥ |
yena bhāryā hṛtā pūrvaṃ kṛtodvāhaḥ parasya vai ||
5.37.d:
पाणिग्रहणमन्त्राणां विघ्रं चक्रे महात्मभिः ।
येन भार्या हृता पूर्वं कृतोद्वाहः परस्य वै ॥
5.37.m: He caused an interruption in the marriage rites by noble men; / by him a wife was previously abducted whose marriage to another had already been performed.

5.37.s:
balātkāmācca mohācca saṃharṣācca yadotkaṭāt |
jahāra kanyāṃ kāmācca kasyacitpuravāsinaḥ ||
5.37.d:
बलात्कामाच्च मोहाच्च संहर्षाच्च यदोत्कटात् ।
जहार कन्यां कामाच्च कस्यचित्पुरवासिनः ॥
5.37.m: When, by force, lust, delusion, and intense insolence, / he seized the maiden of a certain city-dweller out of lust,

5.37.s:
adharmasaṅginaṃ taṃ tu rājā trayyāruṇistyajan |
apadhvaṃseti bahuśo'vadatkrodhasamanvitaḥ ||
5.37.d:
अधर्मसङ्गिनं तं तु राजा त्रय्यारुणिस्त्यजन् ।
अपध्वंसेति बहुशोऽवदत्क्रोधसमन्वितः ॥
5.37.m: King Trayyāruṇi, renouncing him who was clinging to adharma, / repeatedly said, filled with anger: “Perish!”

5.37.s:
pitaraṃ so'bravīnd duṣṭaḥ kva gacchāmīti vai tadā |
vasa śvapākanikaṭe rājā prāheti taṃ tadā ||
5.37.d:
पितरं सोऽब्रवीन्द् दुष्टः क्व गच्छामीति वै तदा ।
वस श्वपाकनिकटे राजा प्राहेति तं तदा ॥
5.37.m: The wicked one said to his father: “Where, then, shall I go?” / The king then said to him: “Live near the dog-cookers!”

5.37.s:
sa hi satyavratastena śvapākavasathāntike |
pitrā tyakto'vasadvīro dharmapālena bhūbhujā ||
5.37.d:
स हि सत्यव्रतस्तेन श्वपाकवसथान्तिके ।
पित्रा त्यक्तोऽवसद्वीरो धर्मपालेन भूभुजा ॥
5.37.m: Abandoned by his father, the king who was a protector of dharma, / that hero Satyavrata dwelt near the settlements of dog-cookers.

5.37.s:
tatastrayyāruṇī rājā viraktaḥ putrakarmaṇā |
sa śaṅkaratapaḥ kartuṃ sarvaṃ tyaktvā vanaṃ yayau ||
5.37.d:
ततस्त्रय्यारुणी राजा विरक्तः पुत्रकर्मणा ।
स शङ्करतपः कर्तुं सर्वं त्यक्त्वा वनं ययौ ॥
5.37.m: Then King Trayyāruṇi, disgusted by his son's deed, / abandoned everything and went to the forest to perform austerity to Śaṅkara.

5.37.s:
tatastasya svaviṣaye nāvarṣatpākaśāsanaḥ |
samā dvādaśa viprarṣe tenādharmeṇa vai tadā ||
5.37.d:
ततस्तस्य स्वविषये नावर्षत्पाकशासनः ।
समा द्वादश विप्रर्षे तेनाधर्मेण वै तदा ॥
5.37.m: Then Indra did not rain upon his realm / for twelve years, O sage among the twice-born, on account of that adharma.

5.37.s:
dārāṃstasya tu viṣaye viśvāmitro mahātapāḥ |
santyajya sāgarānūpe cacāra vipulaṃ tapaḥ ||
5.37.d:
दारांस्तस्य तु विषये विश्वामित्रो महातपाः ।
सन्त्यज्य सागरानूपे चचार विपुलं तपः ॥
5.37.m: Having abandoned his wife in that realm, Viśvāmitra of great austerity / performed vast austerity on the shore of the ocean.

5.37.s:
tasya patnī gale baddhvā madhyamaṃ putramaurasam |
śeṣasya bharaṇārthāya vyakrīṇādgośatena ca ||
5.37.d:
तस्य पत्नी गले बद्ध्वा मध्यमं पुत्रमौरसम् ।
शेषस्य भरणार्थाय व्यक्रीणाद्गोशतेन च ॥
5.37.m: Tying a cord around the neck of her middle biological son, his wife / sold him for a hundred cows to maintain the rest [of the family].

5.37.s:
tāṃ tu dṛṣṭvā gale baddhaṃ vikrīṇantīṃ svamātmajam |
maharṣiputraṃ dharmātmā mocayāmāsa taṃ tadā ||
5.37.d:
तां तु दृष्ट्वा गले बद्धं विक्रीणन्तीं स्वमात्मजम् ।
महर्षिपुत्रं धर्मात्मा मोचयामास तं तदा ॥
5.37.m:
Seeing her selling her own son bound by the neck,
the righteous-minded prince then freed that son of the great sage.

5.37.s:
satyavrato mahābāhurbharaṇaṃ tasya cākarot |
viśvāmitrasya tuṣṭyarthamanukrośārthameva ca ||
5.37.d:
सत्यव्रतो महाबाहुर्भरणं तस्य चाकरोत् ।
विश्वामित्रस्य तुष्ट्यर्थमनुक्रोशार्थमेव च ॥
5.37.m:
Mighty-armed Satyavrata also provided maintenance for him,
for the pleasure of Viśvāmitra and out of compassion.

5.37.s:
tadārabhya sa putrastu viśvāmitrasya vai muneḥ |
abhavadgālavo nāma galabandhānmahātapāḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.37.d:
तदारभ्य स पुत्रस्तु विश्वामित्रस्य वै मुनेः ।
अभवद्गालवो नाम गलबन्धान्महातपाः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.37.m:
From that time on, that son of the sage Viśvāmitra,
a man of great austerity, became known indeed as Gālava, from the binding around the neck.

Homage to glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.38.s:
sūta uvāca |
satyavratastu tadbhaktyā kṛpayā ca pratijñayā |
viśvāmitrakalatraṃ ca poṣayāmāsa vai tadā ||
5.38.d:
सूत उवाच ।
सत्यव्रतस्तु तद्भक्त्या कृपया च प्रतिज्ञया ।
विश्वामित्रकलत्रं च पोषयामास वै तदा ॥
5.38.m:
Sūta said:
Out of devotion to him, out of pity, and by his vow,
Satyavrata then indeed maintained the wife of Viśvāmitra.

5.38.s:
hatvā mṛgānvarāhāṃśca mahiṣāṃśca vanecarān |
viśvāmitrāśramābhyāśe tanmāṃsaṃ cākṣipanmune ||
5.38.d:
हत्वा मृगान्वराहांश्च महिषांश्च वनेचरान् ।
विश्वामित्राश्रमाभ्याशे तन्मांसं चाक्षिपन्मुने ॥
5.38.m:
Having slain deer, boars, and forest-dwelling buffaloes,
he placed their meat near Viśvāmitra's hermitage, O sage.

5.38.s:
tīrthaṃ gāṃ caiva gātraṃ ca tathaivāntaḥpuraṃ muniḥ |
yājyopādhyāyasaṃyogādvasiṣṭhaḥ paryarakṣata ||
5.38.d:
तीर्थं गां चैव गात्रं च तथैवान्तःपुरं मुनिः ।
याज्योपाध्यायसंयोगाद्वसिष्ठः पर्यरक्षत ॥
5.38.m:
The sacred ford, the cow, the body, and likewise the inner apartments,
the sage Vasiṣṭha protected, due to the connection between patron and priest.

5.38.s:
satyavratasya vākyādvā bhāvino'rthasya vai balāt |
vasiṣṭho'bhyadhikaṃ manyuṃ dhārayāmāsa nityaśaḥ ||
5.38.d:
सत्यव्रतस्य वाक्याद्वा भाविनोऽर्थस्य वै बलात् ।
वसिष्ठोऽभ्यधिकं मन्युं धारयामास नित्यशः ॥
5.38.m:
Whether from the words of Satyavrata or by the force of what was destined to happen,
Vasiṣṭha constantly bore intense anger [against him].

5.38.s:
pitrā tu taṃ tadā rāṣṭrātparityaktaṃ svamātmajam |
na vārayāmāsa munirvasiṣṭhaḥ kāraṇena ca ||
5.38.d:
पित्रा तु तं तदा राष्ट्रात्परित्यक्तं स्वमात्मजम् ।
न वारयामास मुनिर्वसिष्ठः कारणेन च ॥
5.38.m:
When he, his own son, was banished from the realm by his father,
the sage Vasiṣṭha did not prevent it, and that for a reason.

5.38.s:
pāṇigrahaṇamantrāṇāṃ niṣṭhā syātsaptame pade |
na ca satyavratastasya tamupāṃśumabuddhyata ||
5.38.d:
पाणिग्रहणमन्त्राणां निष्ठा स्यात्सप्तमे पदे ।
न च सत्यव्रतस्तस्य तमुपांशुमबुद्ध्यत ॥
5.38.m:
The completion of the marriage mantras occurs at the seventh step;
and Satyavrata did not comprehend that secret whisper of his.

5.38.s:
tasminsa paritoṣāya piturāsīnmahātmanaḥ |
kulasya niṣkṛtirvipra kṛtā sā vai bhavediti ||
5.38.d:
तस्मिन्स परितोषाय पितुरासीन्महात्मनः ।
कुलस्य निष्कृतिर्विप्र कृता सा वै भवेदिति ॥
5.38.m:
“He should be for the satisfaction of his great-souled father;
[thus] that expiation of the family will indeed be accomplished, O brahmin.”

5.38.s:
na taṃ vasiṣṭho bhagavānpitrā tyaktaṃ nyavārayat |
abhiṣekṣyāmyahaṃ putramasya naivābravīnmuniḥ ||
5.38.d:
न तं वसिष्ठो भगवान्पित्रा त्यक्तं न्यवारयत् ।
अभिषेक्ष्याम्यहं पुत्रमस्य नैवाब्रवीन्मुनिः ॥
5.38.m:
The lordly Vasiṣṭha did not prevent him when he was cast out by his father;
the sage did not say, “I shall consecrate his son.”

5.38.s:
sa tu dvādaśa varṣāṇi dīkṣāṃ tāmudvahad balī |
avidyāmāne māṃse tu vasiṣṭhasya mahātmanaḥ ||
5.38.d:
स तु द्वादश वर्षाणि दीक्षां तामुद्वहद् बली ।
अविद्यामाने मांसे तु वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ॥
5.38.m:
The mighty prince bore that initiation for twelve years.
Then, when no meat was to be found, [the milch cow] of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha—

5.38.s:
sarvakāmaduhāṃ dogdhrīṃ dadarśa sa nṛpātmajaḥ |
tāṃ vai krodhācca lobhācca śramādvai ca kṣudhānvitaḥ ||
5.38.d:
सर्वकामदुहां दोग्ध्रीं ददर्श स नृपात्मजः ।
तां वै क्रोधाच्च लोभाच्च श्रमाद्वै च क्षुधान्वितः ॥
5.38.m:
that milch cow yielding all desires, the king's son saw.
Overcome with hunger, out of anger, greed, and weariness,

5.38.s:
dāśadharmagato rājā tāṃ jaghāna sa vai mune |
sa taṃ māṃsaṃ svayaṃ caiva viśvāmitrasya cātmajam ||
5.38.d:
दाशधर्मगतो राजा तां जघान स वै मुने ।
स तं मांसं स्वयं चैव विश्वामित्रस्य चात्मजम् ॥
5.38.m:
acting in the manner of a fisherman, the prince slew her, O sage.
He himself [ate] that meat, and also Viśvāmitra's son

5.38.s:
bhojayāmāsa tacchrutvā vasiṣṭho hyasya cukrudhe |
uvāca ca muniśreṣṭhastaṃ tadā krodhasaṃyutaḥ ||
5.38.d:
भोजयामास तच्छ्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो ह्यस्य चुक्रुधे ।
उवाच च मुनिश्रेष्ठस्तं तदा क्रोधसंयुतः ॥
5.38.m:
he fed. Hearing of that, Vasiṣṭha became enraged at him,
and the best of sages, filled with wrath, then said to him:

5.38.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca |
pātayeyamahaṃ krūra tava śaṅkumaśaṃsayam |
yadi te dvāvimau śaṅkū nasyātāṃ vai kṛtau purā ||
5.38.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच ।
पातयेयमहं क्रूर तव शङ्कुमशंसयम् ।
यदि ते द्वाविमौ शङ्कू नस्यातां वै कृतौ पुरा ॥
5.38.m:
Vasiṣṭha said:
“Cruel one, I would undoubtedly remove your peg,
if these two pegs had not indeed been made by you before.

5.38.s:
pituścāparitoṣeṇa gurordogdhrīvadhena ca |
aprokṣitopayogācca trividhaste vyatikramaḥ ||
5.38.d:
पितुश्चापरितोषेण गुरोर्दोग्ध्रीवधेन च ।
अप्रोक्षितोपयोगाच्च त्रिविधस्ते व्यतिक्रमः ॥
5.38.m:
By your father's displeasure, by the slaughter of your guru's milch cow,
and by the consumption of unsprinkled [meat], threefold is your transgression.”

5.38.s:
triśaṅkuriti hovāca triśaṅkuriti sa smṛtaḥ |
viśvāmitrastu dārāṇāmāgato bharaṇe kṛte ||
5.38.d:
त्रिशङ्कुरिति होवाच त्रिशङ्कुरिति स स्मृतः ।
विश्वामित्रस्तु दाराणामागतो भरणे कृते ॥
5.38.m:
“Triśaṅku (he of three sins),” he called him; thus he is remembered as Triśaṅku.
Viśvāmitra, however, returned once the maintenance of his wives had been accomplished.

5.38.s:
tena tasmai varaṃ prādānmuniḥ prītastriśaṅkave |
chandyamāno vareṇātha varaṃ vavre nṛpātmajaḥ ||
5.38.d:
तेन तस्मै वरं प्रादान्मुनिः प्रीतस्त्रिशङ्कवे ।
छन्द्यमानो वरेणाथ वरं वव्रे नृपात्मजः ॥
5.38.m:
Pleased, the sage granted a boon to that Triśaṅku for that [deed].
Being invited with a boon, the king's son then chose a boon.

5.38.s:
anāvṛṣṭibhaye cāsmiñjāte dvādaśavārṣike |
abhiṣicya pitū rājye yājayāmāsa taṃ muniḥ ||
5.38.d:
अनावृष्टिभये चास्मिञ्जाते द्वादशवार्षिके ।
अभिषिच्य पितू राज्ये याजयामास तं मुनिः ॥
5.38.m:
When this twelve-year dread of drought had arisen,
having consecrated him in his father's kingdom, the sage performed a sacrifice for him.

5.38.s:
miṣatāṃ devatānāṃ ca vasiṣṭhasya ca kauśikaḥ |
saśarīraṃ tadā taṃ tu divamārohayatprabhuḥ ||
5.38.d:
मिषतां देवतानां च वसिष्ठस्य च कौशिकः ।
सशरीरं तदा तं तु दिवमारोहयत्प्रभुः ॥
5.38.m:
Before the very eyes of the gods and Vasiṣṭha, the powerful Kauśika
then caused him to ascend to heaven in his physical body.

5.38.s:
tasya satyarathā nāma bhāryā kekayavaṃśajā |
kumāraṃ janayāmāsa hariścandramakalmaṣam ||
5.38.d:
तस्य सत्यरथा नाम भार्या केकयवंशजा ।
कुमारं जनयामास हरिश्चन्द्रमकल्मषम् ॥
5.38.m:
His wife, named Satyarathā, born of the Kekaya lineage,
gave birth to a spotless prince, Hariścandra.

5.38.s:
sa vai rājā hariścandro traiśaṅkava iti smṛtaḥ |
āhartā rājasūyasya samrāḍiti ha viśrutaḥ ||
5.38.d:
स वै राजा हरिश्चन्द्रो त्रैशङ्कव इति स्मृतः ।
आहर्ता राजसूयस्य सम्राडिति ह विश्रुतः ॥
5.38.m:
That king Hariścandra is remembered as the son of Triśaṅku,
the performer of the Rājasūya sacrifice, renowned as an emperor.

5.38.s:
hariścandrasya hi suto rohito nāma viśrutaḥ |
rohitasya vṛkaḥ putro vṛkād bāhustu jajñivān ||
5.38.d:
हरिश्चन्द्रस्य हि सुतो रोहितो नाम विश्रुतः ।
रोहितस्य वृकः पुत्रो वृकाद् बाहुस्तु जज्ञिवान् ॥
5.38.m:
Hariścandra's son is renowned by the name Rohita;
Rohita's son was Vṛka, and from Vṛka, Bāhu was born.

5.38.s:
haihayāstālajaṅghāśca nirasyanti sma taṃ nṛpam |
nātyarthe dhārmiko viprāḥ sa hi dharmayuge'bhavat ||
5.38.d:
हैहयास्तालजङ्घाश्च निरस्यन्ति स्म तं नृपम् ।
नात्यर्थे धार्मिको विप्राः स हि धर्मयुगेऽभवत् ॥
5.38.m:
The Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas drove out that king.
He was not exceedingly righteous, O brahmins, though he lived in the age of righteousness.

5.38.s:
sagaraṃ sa sutaṃ bāhurjajñe saha gareṇa vai |
aurvasyāśramamāsādya bhārgaveṇābhirakṣitaḥ ||
5.38.d:
सगरं स सुतं बाहुर्जज्ञे सह गरेण वै ।
और्वस्याश्रममासाद्य भार्गवेणाभिरक्षितः ॥
5.38.m:
Bāhu begot a son, Sagara, along with poison (gara);
having reached Aurva's hermitage, he was protected by the descendant of Bhṛgu.

5.38.s:
āgneyamastraṃ labdhvā ca bhārgavātsagaro nṛpaḥ |
jigāya pṛthivīṃ hatvā tālajaṅghānsa haihayāna ||
5.38.d:
आग्नेयमस्त्रं लब्ध्वा च भार्गवात्सगरो नृपः ।
जिगाय पृथिवीं हत्वा तालजङ्घान्स हैहयान ॥
5.38.m:
Having obtained the fire-weapon from the descendant of Bhṛgu, King Sagara
conquered the earth, slaying the Tālajaṅghas and the Haihayas,

5.38.s:
śakānbahūdakāṃścaiva pāradānsagaṇānkhaśān |
sudharmaṃ sthāpayāmāsa śaśāsa vṛṣataḥ kṣitim ||
5.38.d:
शकान्बहूदकांश्चैव पारदान्सगणान्खशान् ।
सुधर्मं स्थापयामास शशास वृषतः क्षितिम् ॥
5.38.m:
the Śakas, the Bahūdakas, the Pāradas, along with the hosts of Khaśas.
He established good righteousness and ruled the earth in accordance with virtue.

5.38.s:
śaunaka uvāca |
sa vai gareṇa sahitaḥ kathaṃ jātastu kṣatriyāt |
jitavānetadācakṣva vistareṇa hi sūtaja ||
5.38.d:
शौनक उवाच ।
स वै गरेण सहितः कथं जातस्तु क्षत्रियात् ।
जितवानेतदाचक्ष्व विस्तरेण हि सूतज ॥
5.38.m:
Śaunaka said:
How was he born from a kṣatriya along with poison?
Tell in full how he conquered [them], O son of Sūta.

5.38.s:
sūta uvāca |
pārīkṣitena sampṛṣṭo vaiśampāyana eva ca |
yadācaṣṭa sma tadvakṣye śṛṇuṣvaikamanā mune ||
5.38.d:
सूत उवाच ।
पारीक्षितेन सम्पृष्टो वैशम्पायन एव च ।
यदाचष्ट स्म तद्वक्ष्ये शृणुष्वैकमना मुने ॥
5.38.m:
Sūta said:
What Vaiśampāyana declared when questioned by the son of Parīkṣit,
that I shall tell; listen with one-pointed mind, O sage.

5.38.s:
parīkṣitovāca |
kathaṃ sa sagaro rājā gareṇa sahito mune |
jātaḥ sa jaghnivānbhūpānetadākhyātumarhasi ||
5.38.d:
परीक्षितोवाच ।
कथं स सगरो राजा गरेण सहितो मुने ।
जातः स जघ्निवान्भूपानेतदाख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
5.38.m:
Parīkṣit said:
How was that King Sagara born along with poison, O sage,
and how did he slay the kings? Be pleased to relate this.

5.38.s:
vaiśampāyana uvāca |
bāhorvyasaninastātahṛtaṃ rājyamabhūtkila |
haihayaistālajaṅghaiśca śakaiḥ sārdhaṃ viśāmpate ||
5.38.d:
वैशम्पायन उवाच ।
बाहोर्व्यसनिनस्तातहृतं राज्यमभूत्किल ।
हैहयैस्तालजङ्घैश्च शकैः सार्धं विशाम्पते ॥
5.38.m:
Vaiśampāyana said:
The kingdom of Bāhu, who had fallen into misfortune, was seized, O dear one,
by the Haihayas and the Tālajaṅghas, together with the Śakas, O ruler of the people.

5.38.s:
yavanāḥ pāradāścaiva kāmbojāḥ pāhlavāstathā |
bahūdakāśca pañcaiva gaṇāḥ proktāśca rakṣasām ||
5.38.d:
यवनाः पारदाश्चैव काम्बोजाः पाह्लवास्तथा ।
बहूदकाश्च पञ्चैव गणाः प्रोक्ताश्च रक्षसाम् ॥
5.38.m:
The Yavanas, the Pāradas, the Kāmbojas, and likewise the Pahlavas,
and the Bahūdakas—these five hosts of monsters are mentioned.

5.38.s:
ete pañca gaṇā rājan haihayārtheṣu rakṣasām |
kṛtvā parākramān bāho rājyaṃ tebhyo dadurbalāt ||
5.38.d:
एते पञ्च गणा राजन् हैहयार्थेषु रक्षसाम् ।
कृत्वा पराक्रमान् बाहो राज्यं तेभ्यो ददुर्बलात् ॥
5.38.m:
These five hosts of monsters, O king, on behalf of the Haihayas,
having displayed their valor, forcibly gave Bāhu's kingdom to them.

5.38.s:
hatarājyastato rājā sa vai bāhurvanaṃ yayau |
patnyā cānugato duḥkhī sa vai prāṇānavāsṛjat ||
5.38.d:
हतराज्यस्ततो राजा स वै बाहुर्वनं ययौ ।
पत्न्या चानुगतो दुःखी स वै प्राणानवासृजत् ॥
5.38.m:
Then the king, his realm destroyed, that Bāhu went to the forest;
followed by his wife, sorrowful, he gave up his life.

5.38.s:
patnī yā yādavī tasya sagarbhā pṛṣṭhato gatā |
sapatnyā ca garastasyai dattaḥ pūrvasuterṣyayā ||
5.38.d:
पत्नी या यादवी तस्य सगर्भा पृष्ठतो गता ।
सपत्न्या च गरस्तस्यै दत्तः पूर्वसुतेर्ष्यया ॥
5.38.m:
His wife, a Yādava princess, followed behind him while pregnant;
and poison had been administered to her by a co-wife out of jealousy over a previous son.

5.38.s:
sā tu bhartuścitāṃ kṛtvā jvalanaṃ cāvarohata |
aurvastāṃ bhārgavo rājankāruṇyātsamavārayat ||
5.38.d:
सा तु भर्तुश्चितां कृत्वा ज्वलनं चावरोहत ।
और्वस्तां भार्गवो राजन्कारुण्यात्समवारयत् ॥
5.38.m:
She prepared a funeral pyre for her husband and descended into the fire;
Aurva, the descendant of Bhṛgu, O king, restrained her out of compassion.

5.38.s:
tasyāśrame sthitā rājñī garbharakṣaṇahetave |
siṣeve munivaryaṃ taṃ smarantī śaṅkaraṃ hṛdā ||
5.38.d:
तस्याश्रमे स्थिता राज्ञी गर्भरक्षणहेतवे ।
सिषेवे मुनिवर्यं तं स्मरन्ती शङ्करं हृदा ॥
5.38.m:
Remaining in his hermitage for the purpose of protecting her unborn child,
the queen served that best of sages, remembering Śaṅkara in her heart.

5.38.s:
ekadā khalu tad garbho gareṇaiva saha cyutaḥ |
sumuhūrtte sulagne ca pañcoccagrahasaṃyute ||
5.38.d:
एकदा खलु तद् गर्भो गरेणैव सह च्युतः ।
सुमुहूर्त्ते सुलग्ने च पञ्चोच्चग्रहसंयुते ॥
5.38.m:
Then, one day, that fetus was delivered along with the poison itself,
at an auspicious hour and an auspicious astrological ascendant, joined by five exalted planets.

5.38.s:
tasmim̐llagne ca balini sarvathā munisattama |
vyajāyata mahābāhuḥ sagaro nāma pārthivaḥ ||
5.38.d:
तस्मिम्̐ल्लग्ने च बलिनि सर्वथा मुनिसत्तम ।
व्यजायत महाबाहुः सगरो नाम पार्थिवः ॥
5.38.m:
At that powerful ascendant, O best of sages,
was born the mighty-armed monarch named Sagara.

5.38.s:
aurvastu jātakarmādi tasya kṛtvā mahātmanaḥ |
adhyāpya vedaśāstrāṇi tato'straṃ pratyapādayat ||
5.38.d:
और्वस्तु जातकर्मादि तस्य कृत्वा महात्मनः ।
अध्याप्य वेदशास्त्राणि ततोऽस्त्रं प्रत्यपादयत् ॥
5.38.m:
Aurva performed the birth rites and others for that great-souled prince;
having taught him the Vedas and the treatises, he then imparted the weapon to him.

5.38.s:
āgneyaṃ taṃ mahābhāgo hyamarairapi duḥsaham |
jagrāha vidhinā prītyā sagaro'sau nṛpottamaḥ ||
5.38.d:
आग्नेयं तं महाभागो ह्यमरैरपि दुःसहम् ।
जग्राह विधिना प्रीत्या सगरोऽसौ नृपोत्तमः ॥
5.38.m:
That illustrious, best of kings, Sagara, received with joy
according to the rule the fire-weapon, difficult even for the immortals to endure.

5.38.s:
sa tenāstrabalenaiva balena ca samanvitaḥ |
haihayānvijaghānāśu saṅkruddho'strabalena ca ||
5.38.d:
स तेनास्त्रबलेनैव बलेन च समन्वितः ।
हैहयान्विजघानाशु सङ्क्रुद्धोऽस्त्रबलेन च ॥
5.38.m:
Endowed with strength and by the very power of that weapon,
enraged, he swiftly slew the Haihayas by the power of his weapon.

5.38.s:
ājahāra ca lokeṣu kīrtiṃ kīrtimatāṃ varaḥ |
dharmaṃ saṃsthāpayāmāsa sagaro'sau mahītale ||
5.38.d:
आजहार च लोकेषु कीर्तिं कीर्तिमतां वरः ।
धर्मं संस्थापयामास सगरोऽसौ महीतले ॥
5.38.m:
The best among the renowned won fame throughout the worlds;
that Sagara established righteousness on the face of the earth.

5.38.s:
tataḥ śakāḥ sayavanāḥ kāmbojāḥ pāhlavāstathā |
hanyamānāstadā te tu vasiṣṭhaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ ||
5.38.d:
ततः शकाः सयवनाः काम्बोजाः पाह्लवास्तथा ।
हन्यमानास्तदा ते तु वसिष्ठं शरणं ययुः ॥
5.38.m:
Then the Śakas, together with the Yavanas, the Kāmbojas, and the Pahlavas,
being slain at that time, went to Vasiṣṭha for refuge.

5.38.s:
vasiṣṭho vañcanāṃ kṛtvā samayena mahādyutiḥ |
sagaraṃ vārayāmāsa teṣāṃ datvābhayaṃ nṛpam ||
5.38.d:
वसिष्ठो वञ्चनां कृत्वा समयेन महाद्युतिः ।
सगरं वारयामास तेषां दत्वाभयं नृपम् ॥
5.38.m: The resplendent Vasiṣṭha, having devised an agreement by a stratagem, / restrained King Sagara after granting them protection from fear.

5.38.s:
sagaraḥ svāṃ pratijñāṃ tu gurorvākyaṃ niśamya ca |
dharmaṃ jaghāna teṣāṃ vai keśānyatvaṃ cakāra ha ||
5.38.d:
सगरः स्वां प्रतिज्ञां तु गुरोर्वाक्यं निशम्य च ।
धर्मं जघान तेषां वै केशान्यत्वं चकार ह ॥
5.38.m: Sagara, however, having heard his guru's words, and [keeping] his own pledge, / destroyed their duty and altered their hair.

5.38.s:
ardhaṃ śakānāṃ śiraso muṇḍaṃ kṛtvā vyasarjayat |
yavanānāṃ śiraḥ sarvaṃ kāmbojānāṃ tathaiva ca ||
5.38.d:
अर्धं शकानां शिरसो मुण्डं कृत्वा व्यसर्जयत् ।
यवनानां शिरः सर्वं काम्बोजानां तथैव च ॥
5.38.m: Having shaved half the head of the Śakas, he released them, / and the entire head of the Yavanas and the Kāmbojas likewise.

5.38.s:
pāradā muṇḍakeśāśca pāhnavāśśmaśrudhāriṇaḥ |
niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkārāḥ kṛtāstena mahātmanā ||
5.38.d:
पारदा मुण्डकेशाश्च पाह्नवाश्श्मश्रुधारिणः ।
निःस्वाध्यायवषट्काराः कृतास्तेन महात्मना ॥
5.38.m: The Pāradas were made to shave their hair, and the Pāhnavas to wear beards; / by that great-souled one they were deprived of Vedic recitation and the vaṣaṭ-call.

5.38.s:
jitā ca sakalā pṛthvī dharmatastena bhūbhujā |
sarve te kṣatriyāstāta dharmahīnāḥ kṛtāḥ purā ||
5.38.d:
जिता च सकला पृथ्वी धर्मतस्तेन भूभुजा ।
सर्वे ते क्षत्रियास्तात धर्महीनाः कृताः पुरा ॥
5.38.m: And the entire earth was conquered righteously by that king; / all those kṣatriyas, dear one, were formerly stripped of their duties.

5.38.s:
sa dharmavijayī rājā vijitvemāṃ vasundharām |
aśvaṃ saṃskārayāmāsa vājimedhāya pārthivaḥ ||
5.38.d:
स धर्मविजयी राजा विजित्वेमां वसुन्धराम् ।
अश्वं संस्कारयामास वाजिमेधाय पार्थिवः ॥
5.38.m: Having conquered this earth, that king, victorious through righteousness, / consecrated a horse for the horse sacrifice.

5.38.s:
tasya cārayataḥ so'śvaḥ samudre pūrvadakṣiṇe |
gataḥ ṣaṣṭisahasraistu tatputrairanvito mune ||
5.38.d:
तस्य चारयतः सोऽश्वः समुद्रे पूर्वदक्षिणे ।
गतः षष्टिसहस्रैस्तु तत्पुत्रैरन्वितो मुने ॥
5.38.m: As it roamed, that horse went toward the south-eastern sea, / accompanied by his sixty thousand sons, O sage.

5.38.s:
devarājena śakreṇa so'śvo hi svārthasādhinā |
velāsamīpe'pahṛto bhūmiṃ caiva praveśitaḥ ||
5.38.d:
देवराजेन शक्रेण सोऽश्वो हि स्वार्थसाधिना ।
वेलासमीपेऽपहृतो भूमिं चैव प्रवेशितः ॥
5.38.m: Indeed, that horse was stolen near the shore by Śakra, king of the gods, / pursuing his own ends, and was made to enter the earth.

5.38.s:
mahārājo'tha sagarastaddhayānveṣaṇāya ca |
sa taṃ deśaṃ tadā putraiḥ khānayāmāsa sarvataḥ ||
5.38.d:
महाराजोऽथ सगरस्तद्धयान्वेषणाय च ।
स तं देशं तदा पुत्रैः खानयामास सर्वतः ॥
5.38.m: Then Mahārāja Sagara, in order to search for the horse, / had that region excavated on all sides by his sons.

5.38.s:
āseduste tatastatra khanyamāne mahārṇave |
tamādipuruṣaṃ devaṃ kapilaṃ viśvarūpiṇam ||
5.38.d:
आसेदुस्ते ततस्तत्र खन्यमाने महार्णवे ।
तमादिपुरुषं देवं कपिलं विश्वरूपिणम् ॥
5.38.m: Then, as the great ocean was being dug, / they came upon that primordial person, the god Kapila, whose form is the universe.

5.38.s:
tasya cakṣuḥsamutthena vahninā pratibudhyataḥ |
dagdhāḥ ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi catvārastvavaśeṣitāḥ ||
5.38.d:
तस्य चक्षुःसमुत्थेन वह्निना प्रतिबुध्यतः ।
दग्धाः षष्टिसहस्राणि चत्वारस्त्ववशेषिताः ॥
5.38.m: By the fire rising from his eye as he awoke, / the sixty thousand were burned; only four remained.

5.38.s:
harṣaketuḥ suketuśca tathā dharmarathoparaḥ |
śūraḥ pañcajanaścaiva tasya vaṃśakarā nṛpāḥ ||
5.38.d:
हर्षकेतुः सुकेतुश्च तथा धर्मरथोपरः ।
शूरः पञ्चजनश्चैव तस्य वंशकरा नृपाः ॥
5.38.m: Harṣaketu, Suketu, and another, Dharmaratha, / and the heroic Pañcajana were the kings who carried on his lineage.

5.38.s:
prādācca tasmai bhagavān hariḥ pañca varānsvayam |
vaṃśaṃ medhāṃ ca kīrtiṃ ca samudraṃ tanayaṃ dhanam ||
5.38.d:
प्रादाच्च तस्मै भगवान् हरिः पञ्च वरान्स्वयम् ।
वंशं मेधां च कीर्तिं च समुद्रं तनयं धनम् ॥
5.38.m: And the blessed lord Hari himself granted him five boons: / lineage, intelligence, fame, the ocean as a son, and wealth.

5.38.s:
sāgaratvaṃ ca lebhe sa karmaṇā tasya tena vai |
taṃ cāśvamedhikaṃ so'śvaṃ samudrādupalabdhavān ||
5.38.d:
सागरत्वं च लेभे स कर्मणा तस्य तेन वै ।
तं चाश्वमेधिकं सोऽश्वं समुद्रादुपलब्धवान् ॥
5.38.m: And it obtained the name Sāgara through that deed of his; / and he recovered that sacrificial horse from the ocean.

5.38.s:
ājahārāśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ sa tu mahāyaśāḥ |
īje śambhuvibhūtīśca devatāstatra suvratāḥ ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.38.d:
आजहाराश्वमेधानां शतं स तु महायशाः ।
ईजे शम्भुविभूतीश्च देवतास्तत्र सुव्रताः ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.38.m:
That king of great fame performed one hundred horse sacrifices; / and there he worshipped the manifestations of Śambhu and the deities faithful to their vows.

Homage to glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.39.s:
śaunaka uvāca |
sagarasyātmajā vīrāḥ kathaṃ jātā mahābalāḥ |
vikrāntāḥ ṣaṣṭisāhasrā vidhanā kena vā vada ||
5.39.d:
शौनक उवाच ।
सगरस्यात्मजा वीराः कथं जाता महाबलाः ।
विक्रान्ताः षष्टिसाहस्रा विधना केन वा वद ॥
5.39.m: Śaunaka said: / How were the mighty, heroic sons of Sagara, / the valiant sixty thousand, born? And tell me, by whom were they destroyed?

5.39.s:
sūta uvāca |
dve patnyo sagarasyāstāṃ tapasā dagdhakilviṣe |
aurvastayorvaraṃ prādāttoṣito munisattamaḥ ||
5.39.d:
सूत उवाच ।
द्वे पत्न्यो सगरस्यास्तां तपसा दग्धकिल्विषे ।
और्वस्तयोर्वरं प्रादात्तोषितो मुनिसत्तमः ॥
5.39.m: Sūta said: / Sagara had two wives whose sins had been burned away by austerity; / Aurva, the best of sages, being pleased, granted the two a boon.

5.39.s:
ṣaṣṭiputrasahasrāṇi ekā vavre tarasvinām |
ekaṃ vaṃśakaraṃ tvekā yatheṣṭaṃ varaśālinī ||
5.39.d:
षष्टिपुत्रसहस्राणि एका वव्रे तरस्विनाम् ।
एकं वंशकरं त्वेका यथेष्टं वरशालिनी ॥
5.39.m: One chose sixty thousand energetic sons, / while the other, blessed with a boon, chose one who would carry on the lineage, according to her desire.

5.39.s:
tatraivāgatya tāṃllabdhvā putrān śūrānbahūṃstadā |
sā caiva suṣuve tumbaṃ bījapūrvaṃ pṛthak kṛtam ||
5.39.d:
तत्रैवागत्य तांल्लब्ध्वा पुत्रान् शूरान्बहूंस्तदा ।
सा चैव सुषुवे तुम्बं बीजपूर्वं पृथक् कृतम् ॥
5.39.m: Having gone there and obtained those many heroic sons, / she then brought forth a gourd filled with seeds that were separated.

5.39.s:
te sarve hi svadhātrībhirvavṛdhuśca yathākramam |
ghṛtapūrṇeṣu kumbheṣu kumārāḥ prītivarddhanāḥ ||
5.39.d:
ते सर्वे हि स्वधात्रीभिर्ववृधुश्च यथाक्रमम् ।
घृतपूर्णेषु कुम्भेषु कुमाराः प्रीतिवर्द्धनाः ॥
5.39.m: All those princes, who increased joy, / were reared in succession by their nurses in jars filled with clarified butter.

5.39.s:
kapilāgnipradagdhānāṃ teṣāṃ tatra mahātmanām |
ekaḥ pañcajano nāma putro rājā babhūva ha ||
5.39.d:
कपिलाग्निप्रदग्धानां तेषां तत्र महात्मनाम् ।
एकः पञ्चजनो नाम पुत्रो राजा बभूव ह ॥
5.39.m: Of those great-souled ones burned by Kapila’s fire, / one son named Pañcajana became king.

5.39.s:
tataḥ pañcajanasyāsīdaṃśumānnāma vīryavān |
dilīpastanayastasya putro yasya bhagīrathaḥ ||
5.39.d:
ततः पञ्चजनस्यासीदंशुमान्नाम वीर्यवान् ।
दिलीपस्तनयस्तस्य पुत्रो यस्य भगीरथः ॥
5.39.m: From Pañcajana was born the mighty Aṃśumat; / his son was Dilīpa, whose son was Bhagīratha.

5.39.s:
yastu gaṅgā saricchreṣṭhāmavātārayata prabhuḥ |
samudramānayaccemāṃ duhitṛtvamakalpayat ||
5.39.d:
यस्तु गङ्गा सरिच्छ्रेष्ठामवातारयत प्रभुः ।
समुद्रमानयच्चेमां दुहितृत्वमकल्पयत् ॥
5.39.m: The powerful one who brought down the Gaṅgā, best of rivers, / and led her to the ocean, making her his daughter.

5.39.s:
bhagīrathasuto rājā śrutasena iti śrutaḥ |
nābhāgastu sutastasya putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ ||
5.39.d:
भगीरथसुतो राजा श्रुतसेन इति श्रुतः ।
नाभागस्तु सुतस्तस्य पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः ॥
5.39.m: The son of Bhagīratha was the king known as Śrutasena; / his son was Nābhāga, a supremely righteous son.

5.39.s:
ambarīṣastu nābhāgiḥ sindhudvīpastato'bhavat |
ayutājittu dāyādaḥ sindhudvīpasya vīryavān ||
5.39.d:
अम्बरीषस्तु नाभागिः सिन्धुद्वीपस्ततोऽभवत् ।
अयुताजित्तु दायादः सिन्धुद्वीपस्य वीर्यवान् ॥
5.39.m: The son of Nābhāga was Ambarīṣa; from him was Sindhudvīpa; / and the mighty heir of Sindhudvīpa was Ayutājit.

5.39.s:
āyutājitsutastvāsīd ṛtuparṇo mahāyaśāḥ |
divyākṣahṛdayajño'sau rājā nalasakho'bhavat ||
5.39.d:
आयुताजित्सुतस्त्वासीद् ऋतुपर्णो महायशाः ।
दिव्याक्षहृदयज्ञोऽसौ राजा नलसखोऽभवत् ॥
5.39.m: The son of Āyutājit was the far-famed Ṛtuparṇa; / knowing the divine secret of dice, that king became the friend of Nala.

5.39.s:
ṛtuparṇasutastvāsīdanuparṇo mahādyutiḥ |
tasya kalmāṣapādo vai nāmnā mitrasahastathā ||
5.39.d:
ऋतुपर्णसुतस्त्वासीदनुपर्णो महाद्युतिः ।
तस्य कल्माषपादो वै नाम्ना मित्रसहस्तथा ॥
5.39.m: The son of Ṛtuparṇa was Anuparṇa, of great splendor; / his [son] was Kalmāṣapāda, also called Mitrasaha.

5.39.s:
kalmāṣapādasya sutaḥ sarvakarmeti viśrutaḥ |
anaraṇyastu putro'bhūdviśrutaḥ sarvaśarmaṇaḥ ||
5.39.d:
कल्माषपादस्य सुतः सर्वकर्मेति विश्रुतः ।
अनरण्यस्तु पुत्रोऽभूद्विश्रुतः सर्वशर्मणः ॥
5.39.m: The son of Kalmāṣapāda was known as Sarvakarman; / and the son of Sarvaśarman was the renowned Anaraṇya.

5.39.s:
anaraṇyasuto rājā vidvānmuṇḍidruho'bhavat |
niṣadhastasya tanayo ratiḥ khaṭvāṅga ityapi ||
5.39.d:
अनरण्यसुतो राजा विद्वान्मुण्डिद्रुहोऽभवत् ।
निषधस्तस्य तनयो रतिः खट्वाङ्ग इत्यपि ॥
5.39.m: The son of Anaraṇya was the learned king Muṇḍidruh; / his son was Niṣadha, and [his son was] Rati, also known as Khaṭvāṅga,

5.39.s:
yena svargādihāgatya muhūrtaṃ prāpya jīvitam |
trayo'pi sañcitā lokā buddhyā satyena cānagha ||
5.39.d:
येन स्वर्गादिहागत्य मुहूर्तं प्राप्य जीवितम् ।
त्रयोऽपि सञ्चिता लोका बुद्ध्या सत्येन चानघ ॥
5.39.m: by whom, having come here from heaven and obtained a lifespan of only a muhūrta, / all three worlds were won through wisdom and truth, O sinless one.

5.39.s:
dīrghabāhuḥ sutastasya raghustasyābhavatsutaḥ |
ajastasya tu putro'bhūttasmāddaśaratho'bhavat ||
5.39.d:
दीर्घबाहुः सुतस्तस्य रघुस्तस्याभवत्सुतः ।
अजस्तस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूत्तस्माद्दशरथोऽभवत् ॥
5.39.m: His son was Dīrghabāhu, and his son was Raghu; / his son was Aja, and from him was born Daśaratha.

5.39.s:
rāmo daśarathājjajñe dharmātmā yo mahāyaśāḥ |
sa viṣṇvaṃśo mahāśaivaḥ paulastyo yena ghātitaḥ ||
5.39.d:
रामो दशरथाज्जज्ञे धर्मात्मा यो महायशाः ।
स विष्ण्वंशो महाशैवः पौलस्त्यो येन घातितः ॥
5.39.m: From Daśaratha was born Rāma, righteous of soul and of great renown; / he was a portion of Viṣṇu, a great Śaiva, by whom the descendant of Pulastya was slain.

5.39.s:
taccaritraṃ ca bahudhā purāṇeṣu pravarṇitam |
rāmāyaṇe prasiddhaṃ hi nātaḥ proktaṃ tu vistarāt ||
5.39.d:
तच्चरित्रं च बहुधा पुराणेषु प्रवर्णितम् ।
रामायणे प्रसिद्धं हि नातः प्रोक्तं तु विस्तरात् ॥
5.39.m: His deeds are described in many ways in the Purāṇas / and are well known in the Rāmāyaṇa; therefore they are not related at length here.

5.39.s:
rāmasya tanayo jajñe kuśa ityapi viśrutaḥ |
atithistu kuśājjajñe niṣadhastasya cātmajaḥ ||
5.39.d:
रामस्य तनयो जज्ञे कुश इत्यपि विश्रुतः ।
अतिथिस्तु कुशाज्जज्ञे निषधस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥
5.39.m: Rāma's son was born, known also as Kuśa; / from Kuśa was born Atithi, and his son was Niṣadha.

5.39.s:
niṣadhasya nalaḥ putro nabhaḥ putro nalasya tu |
nabhasaḥ puṇḍarīkaśca kṣemadhanvā tataḥ smṛtaḥ ||
5.39.d:
निषधस्य नलः पुत्रो नभः पुत्रो नलस्य तु ।
नभसः पुण्डरीकश्च क्षेमधन्वा ततः स्मृतः ॥
5.39.m: The son of Niṣadha was Nala, and the son of Nala was Nabhas; / from Nabhas came Puṇḍarīka, and from him Kṣemadhanvan is remembered.

5.39.s:
kṣemadhanvasutastvāsīddevānīkaḥ pratāpavān |
āsīdahīnagurnāma devānīkātmajaḥ prabhuḥ ||
5.39.d:
क्षेमधन्वसुतस्त्वासीद्देवानीकः प्रतापवान् ।
आसीदहीनगुर्नाम देवानीकात्मजः प्रभुः ॥
5.39.m: The son of Kṣemadhanvan was the powerful Devānīka; / the lord named Ahīnagu was the son of Devānīka.

5.39.s:
ahīnagostu dāyādaḥ sahasvānnāma vīryavān |
vīrasenātmajastasya yaścekṣvākukulodbhavaḥ ||
5.39.d:
अहीनगोस्तु दायादः सहस्वान्नाम वीर्यवान् ।
वीरसेनात्मजस्तस्य यश्चेक्ष्वाकुकुलोद्भवः ॥
5.39.m: The heir of Ahīnagu was the mighty Sahasvat; / his [son] was Vīrasena, an offspring born in the Ikṣvāku race.

5.39.s:
vīrasenasya dāyādaḥ pāriyātro babhūva ha |
tato balākhyastanayaḥ sthalastasmādabhūtsutaḥ ||
5.39.d:
वीरसेनस्य दायादः पारियात्रो बभूव ह ।
ततो बलाख्यस्तनयः स्थलस्तस्मादभूत्सुतः ॥
5.39.m: The heir of Vīrasena was Pāriyātra; / then came his son named Bala; from him came the son Sthala.

5.39.s:
arkāṃśasambhavastasmātputro yakṣaḥ pratāpavān |
tatsutastvaguṇastvāsīttasmādvidhṛtirātmajaḥ ||
5.39.d:
अर्कांशसम्भवस्तस्मात्पुत्रो यक्षः प्रतापवान् ।
तत्सुतस्त्वगुणस्त्वासीत्तस्माद्विधृतिरात्मजः ॥
5.39.m: From him was born a son, Yakṣa, born of a portion of the Sun, full of valor; / his son was Aguṇa, and from him Vidhṛti was the son.

5.39.s:
hiraṇyanābhastatputro yogācāryo babhūva ha |
sa śiṣyo jaiminimunerhyātmavidyāviśāradaḥ ||
5.39.d:
हिरण्यनाभस्तत्पुत्रो योगाचार्यो बभूव ह ।
स शिष्यो जैमिनिमुनेर्ह्यात्मविद्याविशारदः ॥
5.39.m: His son was Hiraṇyanābha, who was a master of yoga; / he was a disciple of the sage Jaimini and skilled in the knowledge of the Self.

5.39.s:
kauśalyo yājñavalkyo'tha yogamadhyātmasaṃjñakam |
yato'dhyagānnṛpavarād hṛdayagranthibhedanam ||
5.39.d:
कौशल्यो याज्ञवल्क्योऽथ योगमध्यात्मसंज्ञकम् ।
यतोऽध्यगान्नृपवराद् हृदयग्रन्थिभेदनम् ॥
5.39.m: From that excellent king, Yājñavalkya of the Kauśala country / learned the yoga named Adhyātma, which cuts the knots of the heart.

5.39.s:
tatsuto puṣyanāmā hi dhruvasaṃjñastadātmajaḥ |
agnivarṇaḥ sutastasya śīghranāmā sutastataḥ ||
5.39.d:
तत्सुतो पुष्यनामा हि ध्रुवसंज्ञस्तदात्मजः ।
अग्निवर्णः सुतस्तस्य शीघ्रनामा सुतस्ततः ॥
5.39.m: His son was named Puṣya, and his son was named Dhruva; / Agnivarṇa was his son, and from him came the son named Śīghra.

5.39.s:
marunnāmā sutastasya yogasiddho babhūva ha |
asāvāste'dyāpi prabhuḥ kalāpagrāmasaṃjñake ||
5.39.d:
मरुन्नामा सुतस्तस्य योगसिद्धो बभूव ह ।
असावास्तेऽद्यापि प्रभुः कलापग्रामसंज्ञके ॥
5.39.m: His son was named Maru, who achieved perfection in yoga; / that lord resides even today in the place called the village of Kalāpa.

5.39.s:
tadvāsibhiśca munibhiḥ kalerante sa eva hi |
punarbhāvayitā naṣṭaṃ sūryavaṃśaṃ viśeṣataḥ ||
5.39.d:
तद्वासिभिश्च मुनिभिः कलेरन्ते स एव हि ।
पुनर्भावयिता नष्टं सूर्यवंशं विशेषतः ॥
5.39.m: At the end of the Kali age, together with the sages residing there, / he indeed will regenerate the destroyed Solar dynasty in particular.

5.39.s:
pṛthuśrutaśca tatputraḥ sandhistasya sutaḥ smṛtaḥ |
amarṣaṇaḥ sutastasya marutvāṃstatsuto'bhavat ||
5.39.d:
पृथुश्रुतश्च तत्पुत्रः सन्धिस्तस्य सुतः स्मृतः ।
अमर्षणः सुतस्तस्य मरुत्वांस्तत्सुतोऽभवत् ॥
5.39.m: Pṛthuśruta was his son, and Sandhi is remembered as his son; / his son was Amarṣaṇa, and his son was Marutvat.

5.39.s:
viśvasāhvaḥ sutastasya tatsuto'bhūtprasenajit |
takṣakastasya tanayaḥ tatsuto hi bṛhadbalaḥ ||
5.39.d:
विश्वसाह्वः सुतस्तस्य तत्सुतोऽभूत्प्रसेनजित् ।
तक्षकस्तस्य तनयः तत्सुतो हि बृहद्बलः ॥
5.39.m: His son was Viśvasāhva, and his son was Prasenajit; / Takṣaka was his son, and his son was Bṛhadbala.

5.39.s:
eta ikṣvākuvaṃśīyā atītāḥ samprakīrtitāḥ |
śṛṇutānāgatānbhūpāṃstadvaṃśyāndharmavittamān ||
5.39.d:
एत इक्ष्वाकुवंशीया अतीताः सम्प्रकीर्तिताः ।
शृणुतानागतान्भूपांस्तद्वंश्यान्धर्मवित्तमान् ॥
5.39.m: These descendants of the Ikṣvāku dynasty of the past have been proclaimed; / listen to the future kings of that lineage, the foremost knowers of righteousness.

5.39.s:
bṛhadbalasya tanayo bhavitā hi bṛhadraṇaḥ |
bṛhadraṇasutastasyorukriyo hi bhaviṣyati ||
5.39.d:
बृहद्बलस्य तनयो भविता हि बृहद्रणः ।
बृहद्रणसुतस्तस्योरुक्रियो हि भविष्यति ॥
5.39.m: The son of Bṛhadbala will be Bṛhadraṇa; / and the son of Bṛhadraṇa will be Urukriya.

5.39.s:
vatsavṛddhaḥ sutastasya prativyomā sutastataḥ |
bhānustattanayo bhāvī divāko vāhinīpatiḥ ||
5.39.d:
वत्सवृद्धः सुतस्तस्य प्रतिव्योमा सुतस्ततः ।
भानुस्तत्तनयो भावी दिवाको वाहिनीपतिः ॥
5.39.m: His son will be Vatsavṛddha, and from him the son will be Prativyoma; / his son will be Bhānu, and Divāka, commander of an army.

5.39.s:
sahadevaḥ sutastasya mahāvīro bhaviṣyati |
tatsuto bṛhadaśvo hi bhānumāṃstatsuto balī ||
5.39.d:
सहदेवः सुतस्तस्य महावीरो भविष्यति ।
तत्सुतो बृहदश्वो हि भानुमांस्तत्सुतो बली ॥
5.39.m: His son will be Sahadeva, a great hero; / his son will indeed be Bṛhadaśva, and his son the mighty Bhānumant.

5.39.s:
suto bhānumato bhāvī pratīkāśvaśca vīryavān |
supratīkaḥ sutastasya bhaviṣyati nṛpottamaḥ ||
5.39.d:
सुतो भानुमतो भावी प्रतीकाश्वश्च वीर्यवान् ।
सुप्रतीकः सुतस्तस्य भविष्यति नृपोत्तमः ॥
5.39.m: The son of Bhānumant will be the heroic Pratīkāśva; / his son will be Supratīka, an excellent king.

5.39.s:
marudevaḥ sutastasya sunakṣatro bhaviṣyati |
tatsutaḥ puṣkarastasyāntarikṣastatsuto dvijāḥ ||
5.39.d:
मरुदेवः सुतस्तस्य सुनक्षत्रो भविष्यति ।
तत्सुतः पुष्करस्तस्यान्तरिक्षस्तत्सुतो द्विजाः ॥
5.39.m: His son will be Marudeva; Sunakṣatra will be [his son]; / his son will be Puṣkara, and his son Antarikṣa, O twice-born ones.

5.39.s:
sutapāstatsuto vīro mitracittasya cātmajaḥ |
bṛhadbhājaḥ sutastasya barhināmā tadātmajaḥ ||
5.39.d:
सुतपास्तत्सुतो वीरो मित्रचित्तस्य चात्मजः ।
बृहद्भाजः सुतस्तस्य बर्हिनामा तदात्मजः ॥
5.39.m: His son will be the heroic Sutapas, and Mitracitta's own son [was born of him]; / his son will be Bṛhadbhāja, and his son named Barhi.

5.39.s:
kṛtañjayaḥ sutastasya tatsuto hi raṇañjayaḥ |
sañjayastu mayastasya tasya śākyo hi cātmajaḥ ||
5.39.d:
कृतञ्जयः सुतस्तस्य तत्सुतो हि रणञ्जयः ।
सञ्जयस्तु मयस्तस्य तस्य शाक्यो हि चात्मजः ॥
5.39.m: His son will be Kṛtañjaya, and his son indeed Raṇañjaya; / Sañjaya was his [son], born of Maya; and Śākya was his son.

5.39.s:
śuddhodastanayastasya lāṅgalastu tadātmajaḥ |
tasya prasenajitputrastatsutaḥ śūdrakāhvayaḥ ||
5.39.d:
शुद्धोदस्तनयस्तस्य लाङ्गलस्तु तदात्मजः ।
तस्य प्रसेनजित्पुत्रस्तत्सुतः शूद्रकाह्वयः ॥
5.39.m: His son will be Śuddhoda, and Lāṅgala his son; / his son will be Prasenajit, and his son named Śūdraka.

5.39.s:
ruṇako bhavitā tasya surathastatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ |
sumitrastatsuto bhāvī vaṃśaniṣṭhānta eva hi ||
5.39.d:
रुणको भविता तस्य सुरथस्तत्सुतः स्मृतः ।
सुमित्रस्तत्सुतो भावी वंशनिष्ठान्त एव हि ॥
5.39.m: Ruṇaka will be his [son], and Suratha is remembered as his son; / Sumitra will be his son, bringing an end to the lineage.

5.39.s:
sumitrānto'nvayo'yaṃ vai ikṣvākūṇāṃ bhaviṣyati |
rājñāṃ vaicitravīryāṇāṃ dharmiṣṭhānāṃ sukarmaṇām ||
5.39.d:
सुमित्रान्तोऽन्वयोऽयं वै इक्ष्वाकूणां भविष्यति ।
राज्ञां वैचित्रवीर्याणां धर्मिष्ठानां सुकर्मणाम् ॥
5.39.m: This lineage of the Ikṣvākus will indeed end with Sumitra— / of kings of manifold valor, most righteous, of noble deeds.

5.39.s:
sumitraṃ prāpya rājānaṃ sa tadvaṃśaḥ śubhaḥ kalau |
saṃsthāṃ prāpsyati tadbrāhme vardhiṣyati punaḥ kṛte ||
5.39.d:
सुमित्रं प्राप्य राजानं स तद्वंशः शुभः कलौ ।
संस्थां प्राप्स्यति तद्ब्राह्मे वर्धिष्यति पुनः कृते ॥
5.39.m: Reaching King Sumitra, that auspicious lineage in the Kaliyuga / will come to an end; and in that related to Brahmā it will flourish again in the Kṛtayuga.

5.39.s:
etadvaivasvate vaṃśe rājāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ |
ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavāḥ prādhānyena prakīrtitāḥ ||
5.39.d:
एतद्वैवस्वते वंशे राजानो भूरिदक्षिणाः ।
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवाः प्राधान्येन प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
5.39.m: Thus in the lineage of Vaivasvata, kings who gave abundant sacrificial gifts, / originating in the Ikṣvāku lineage, have been proclaimed in prominence.

5.39.s:
puṇyeyaṃ paramā sṛṣṭirādityasya vivasvataḥ |
śrāddhadevasya devasya prajānāṃ puṣṭidasya ca ||
5.39.d:
पुण्येयं परमा सृष्टिरादित्यस्य विवस्वतः ।
श्राद्धदेवस्य देवस्य प्रजानां पुष्टिदस्य च ॥
5.39.m: Sacred is this supreme creation of the sun Vivasvant, / Śrāddhadeva, the god who grants nourishment to creatures.

5.39.s:
paṭhan śṛṇvannimāṃ sṛṣṭimādityasya ca mānavaḥ |
prajāvāneti sāyujyamiha bhuktvā sukhaṃ param ||
śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ ||
śrīgaurīśaṅkarābhyāṃ namaḥ ||
śrīśivamahāpurāṇam ||
5.39.d:
पठन् शृण्वन्निमां सृष्टिमादित्यस्य च मानवः ।
प्रजावानेति सायुज्यमिह भुक्त्वा सुखं परम् ॥
श्रीगणेशाय नमः ॥
श्रीगौरीशङ्कराभ्यां नमः ॥
श्रीशिवमहापुराणम् ॥
5.39.m:
Reciting or hearing this creation of the sun, a man, / endowed with offspring, attains communion after enjoying supreme happiness in this world.

Homage to the glorious Gaurī and Śaṅkara.

5.40.s:
vyāsa uvāca |
ityākarṇya śrāddhadevasūryānvayamanuttamam |
paryapṛcchanmuniśreṣṭhaḥ śaunakaḥ sūtamādarāt ||
5.40.d:
व्यास उवाच ।
इत्याकर्ण्य श्राद्धदेवसूर्यान्वयमनुत्तमम् ।
पर्यपृच्छन्मुनिश्रेष्ठः शौनकः सूतमादरात् ॥
5.40.m: Vyāsa said: / Having heard thus of the unequaled lineage of Śrāddhadeva the Sun, / Śaunaka, the best of sages, inquired of Sūta with respect:

5.40.s:
śaunaka uvāca |
sūta sūta cirañjīva vyāsaśiṣya namo'stu te |
śrāvitā paramā divyā kathā paramapāvanī ||
5.40.d:
शौनक उवाच ।
सूत सूत चिरञ्जीव व्यासशिष्य नमोऽस्तु ते ।
श्राविता परमा दिव्या कथा परमपावनी ॥
5.40.m: Śaunaka said: / O Sūta, O Sūta, live long! O disciple of Vyāsa, homage to you! / You have recounted the supreme, divine narrative, supremely purifying.

5.40.s:
tvayā proktaḥ śrāddhadevaḥ sūryaḥ sadvaṃśavardhanaḥ |
saṃśayastatra me jātastaṃ bravīmi tvadagrataḥ ||
5.40.d:
त्वया प्रोक्तः श्राद्धदेवः सूर्यः सद्वंशवर्धनः ।
संशयस्तत्र मे जातस्तं ब्रवीमि त्वदग्रतः ॥
5.40.m: You declared the Sun to be Śrāddhadeva, the enhancer of a noble lineage; / a doubt has arisen in me regarding this, which I speak before you:

5.40.s:
kuto vai śrāddhadevatvamādityasya vivasvataḥ |
śrotumicchāmi tatprītyā chindhi me saṃśayaṃ tvimam ||
5.40.d:
कुतो वै श्राद्धदेवत्वमादित्यस्य विवस्वतः ।
श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्प्रीत्या छिन्धि मे संशयं त्विमम् ॥
5.40.m: Whence indeed is the status of Śrāddhadeva for the sun Vivasvant? / I wish to hear that out of love; sever this doubt of mine.

5.40.s:
śrāddhasyāpi ca māhātmyaṃ tatphalaṃ ca vada prabho |
prītāśca pitaro yena śreyasā yojayanti tam ||
5.40.d:
श्राद्धस्यापि च माहात्म्यं तत्फलं च वद प्रभो ।
प्रीताश्च पितरो येन श्रेयसा योजयन्ति तम् ॥
5.40.m: And tell the eulogy of the śrāddha and its fruit, O lord, / whereby the pleased ancestors unite him with good fortune.

5.40.s:
etacca śrotumicchāmi pitṛṇāṃ sargamuttamam |
kathaya tvaṃ viśeṣeṇa kṛpāṃ kuru mahāmate ||
5.40.d:
एतच्च श्रोतुमिच्छामि पितृणां सर्गमुत्तमम् ।
कथय त्वं विशेषेण कृपां कुरु महामते ॥
5.40.m: And I wish to hear this: the excellent creation of the ancestors; / tell it in detail, show compassion, O highly intelligent one!

5.40.s:
sūta uvāca |
vacmi tatte'khilaṃ prītyā pitṛsargaṃ tu śaunaka |
mārkaṇḍeyena kathitaṃ bhīṣmāya paripṛcchate ||
5.40.d:
सूत उवाच ।
वच्मि तत्तेऽखिलं प्रीत्या पितृसर्गं तु शौनक ।
मार्कण्डेयेन कथितं भीष्माय परिपृच्छते ॥
5.40.m: Sūta said: / I will tell you all that with love, the creation of the ancestors, O Śaunaka, / as told by Mārkaṇḍeya to Bhīṣma when he inquired—

5.40.s:
gītaṃ sanatkumāreṇa mārkaṇḍeyāya dhīmate |
tatte'haṃ sampravakṣyāmi sarvakāmaphalapradam ||
5.40.d:
गीतं सनत्कुमारेण मार्कण्डेयाय धीमते ।
तत्तेऽहं सम्प्रवक्ष्यामि सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
5.40.m: sung by Sanatkumāra to the wise Mārkaṇḍeya; / that I shall fully proclaim to you, granting the fruit of all desires.

5.40.s:
yudhiṣṭhireṇa sampṛṣṭo bhīṣmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ |
śaraśayyāsthitaḥ proce tacchṛṇuṣva vadāmi te ||
5.40.d:
युधिष्ठिरेण सम्पृष्टो भीष्मो धर्मभृतां वरः ।
शरशय्यास्थितः प्रोचे तच्छृणुष्व वदामि ते ॥
5.40.m: Inquired by Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma, the best of the upholders of righteousness, / lying upon a bed of arrows, spoke; hear that, I tell you.

5.40.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca |
puṣṭikāmena puṃsāṃ vai kathaṃ puṣṭiravāpyate |
